options: timing how long reflected sound waves take to return from the seafloor
questions.explain: Sonar uses echoes: distance follows from travel time and the speed of sound in water.

questions.q: As the frequency of a wave increases (with speed constant), its wavelength...
questions.explain: Speed = frequency x wavelength, so higher frequency means shorter wavelength at the same speed.

questions.q: Ultrasound used in medical imaging is...
options: light used to see inside the body
sound with frequencies too high for humans to hear
questions.explain: Ultrasound uses high-frequency sound waves that reflect off internal structures.

questions.q: Which wave needs a medium to travel?
questions.explain: Sound is a mechanical wave needing matter; electromagnetic waves can cross empty space.

questions.q: Which term means: a disturbance that transfers energy through matter or through space?
questions.explain: The term 'wave' means a disturbance that transfers energy through matter or through space.

questions.q: Which term means: the number of complete waves that pass a point in one second, measured in hertz?
questions.explain: The term 'frequency' means the number of complete waves that pass a point in one second, measured in hertz.

questions.q: Which term means: the distance from a wave's resting position to its crest, related to the wave's energy?
questions.explain: The term 'amplitude' means the distance from a wave's resting position to its crest, related to the wave's energy.

questions.q: Which term means: the material substance through which a wave travels?
questions.explain: The term 'medium' means the material substance through which a wave travels.

questions.q: A wave has a frequency of 2 hertz and a wavelength of 3 meters. What is its speed? (speed = frequency x wavelength)
questions.explain: Speed = 2 x 3 = 6 meters per second.

questions.q: A wave has a frequency of 6 hertz and a wavelength of 4 meters. What is its speed? (speed = frequency x wavelength)
questions.explain: Speed = 6 x 4 = 24 meters per second.

questions.q: A student counts 50 complete waves passing a point in 5 seconds. What is the frequency of the waves?
questions.explain: Frequency = waves / time = 50 / 5 = 10 hertz.

questions.q: A student counts 10 complete waves passing a point in 5 seconds. What is the frequency of the waves?
questions.explain: Frequency = waves / time = 10 / 5 = 2 hertz.

rounds.title: Energy, Heat & Waves - Quest 3
rounds.desc: Wave properties, sound, pitch, and echoes.

title: Energy, Heat & Waves - Quest 4
subject: Middle School Science
description: Boss quest: light, reflection, refraction, and the electromagnetic spectrum.

questions.q: Light travels through space in...
options: straight lines, unless it reflects or refracts
questions.explain: Light follows straight-line paths (rays) until it interacts with matter.

questions.q: A pencil in a glass of water looks bent at the surface. This is caused by...
options: refraction - light bends as it passes from water to air
questions.explain: Light changes speed and direction at the water-air boundary, shifting the pencil's apparent position.

questions.q: Mirrors work because of...
options: reflection of light off a smooth surface
questions.explain: Smooth surfaces reflect light in an orderly way, forming images.

questions.q: A white light passed through a prism separates into colors because...
options: light slows to a stop in glass
different wavelengths of light bend by different amounts (dispersion)
the prism adds colors that were not there
questions.explain: Prisms refract each wavelength differently, spreading white light into a spectrum.

questions.q: A material that lets almost all light pass through, like clear glass, is called...
questions.explain: Transparent materials transmit light clearly.

questions.q: Frosted glass that lets light through but blurs images is...
questions.explain: Translucent materials transmit light but scatter it.

questions.q: A wooden door that blocks all light is...
questions.explain: Opaque materials do not transmit light.

questions.q: Which list orders parts of the electromagnetic spectrum from LONGEST wavelength to SHORTEST?
options: radio waves -> visible light -> X-rays -> gamma rays
visible light -> radio waves -> gamma rays -> X-rays
X-rays -> radio waves -> gamma rays -> visible light
gamma rays -> X-rays -> visible light -> radio waves
questions.explain: Radio waves have the longest wavelengths; gamma rays the shortest (and highest frequency).

questions.q: Why does a black shirt feel hotter in sunlight than a white shirt?
options: White shirts block all energy forever
Black fabric produces heat on its own
Black surfaces absorb more light energy and convert it to heat; white surfaces reflect more
questions.explain: Dark colors absorb more radiant energy, warming faster.

questions.q: Ultraviolet (UV) light from the Sun can be harmful because it can...
options: damage skin cells and cause sunburn
questions.explain: UV radiation carries enough energy to damage living cells; sunscreen reduces exposure.

questions.q: A convex lens is useful in eyeglasses and magnifiers because it...
options: reflects light like a mirror only
bends light rays so they converge (come together)
questions.explain: Convex lenses refract light inward, focusing images.

questions.q: Compared with sound waves, light waves...
options: travel much faster and do not need a medium
questions.explain: Light moves at 300,000 kilometers per second in vacuum and needs no medium.

questions.q: Which term means: the bouncing of a wave off the surface of a material?
questions.explain: The term 'reflection' means the bouncing of a wave off the surface of a material.

questions.q: Which term means: the bending of a wave as it passes at an angle from one medium into another?
questions.explain: The term 'refraction' means the bending of a wave as it passes at an angle from one medium into another.

questions.q: What does the term 'electromagnetic spectrum' mean?
options: the distance from a wave's resting position to its crest, related to the wave's energy
the transfer of heat energy through direct contact between materials
the complete range of electromagnetic waves, from radio waves to gamma rays
how high or low a sound seems, which is determined by the sound's frequency
questions.explain: 'Electromagnetic spectrum' means the complete range of electromagnetic waves, from radio waves to gamma rays.

questions.q: Which term means: a region of space that contains no matter at all?
questions.explain: The term 'vacuum' means a region of space that contains no matter at all.

questions.q: Light travels at 300,000 kilometers per second. How long does light take to travel 600000 kilometers?
questions.explain: Time = distance / speed = 600000 / 300,000 = 2 seconds.

questions.q: Light travels at 300,000 kilometers per second. How long does light take to travel 1500000 kilometers?
questions.explain: Time = distance / speed = 1500000 / 300,000 = 5 seconds.

questions.q: A wave has a frequency of 6 hertz and a wavelength of 1 meters. What is its speed? (speed = frequency x wavelength)
questions.explain: Speed = 6 x 1 = 6 meters per second.

questions.q: A wave has a frequency of 5 hertz and a wavelength of 6 meters. What is its speed? (speed = frequency x wavelength)
questions.explain: Speed = 5 x 6 = 30 meters per second.

rounds.title: Energy, Heat & Waves - Quest 4
rounds.desc: Boss quest: light, reflection, refraction, and the electromagnetic spectrum.

title: Earth & Space Science - Quest 1
subject: Middle School Science
description: Earth's layers, tectonic plates, earthquakes, and volcanoes.

questions.q: Which list orders Earth's layers from the surface to the center?
questions.explain: From outside in: the crust, then the mantle, then the core.

questions.q: Which layer of Earth is the thickest?
questions.explain: The mantle extends about 2,900 kilometers down and is Earth's thickest layer.

questions.q: Earth's core is made mostly of...
questions.explain: The core is a dense ball of iron and nickel.

questions.q: What evidence supports the idea that the continents were once joined as Pangaea?
options: Ocean water is the same temperature everywhere
All continents have the same language roots
The continents have the same weather
Identical fossils of land animals are found on continents now separated by oceans, and the coastlines fit together like puzzle pieces
questions.explain: Matching fossils and fitting coastlines on separate continents point to a joined past.

questions.q: What drives the slow movement of tectonic plates?
options: convection currents in the mantle, where hot rock rises and cooler rock sinks
questions.explain: Heat-driven convection in the mantle drags the plates along very slowly.

questions.q: At a convergent boundary where an ocean plate sinks under a continent, you would most likely find...
options: a deep ocean trench and volcanoes
questions.explain: Subduction creates trenches and volcanic mountain chains.

questions.q: New ocean floor is created at...
options: mid-ocean ridges, where plates move apart
questions.explain: Divergent boundaries under the ocean build new crust at mid-ocean ridges.

questions.q: The 'Ring of Fire' around the Pacific Ocean is known for...
options: frequent volcanoes and earthquakes along plate boundaries
questions.explain: Many plate boundaries meet around the Pacific, producing volcanoes and quakes.

questions.q: Which instrument records the vibrations of an earthquake?
questions.explain: Seismographs detect and record seismic waves.

questions.q: Most earthquakes occur...
options: in the centers of plates only
questions.explain: Stress builds where plates meet, and sudden fault movement releases it as quakes.

questions.q: When magma reaches Earth's surface and flows out, it is called...
questions.explain: Magma underground becomes lava once it erupts onto the surface.

questions.q: Which is the best explanation for why the Hawaiian Islands formed in the middle of a plate?
options: A hot spot in the mantle melted through the plate as it moved over the spot
The islands are pieces of a broken continent
questions.explain: Hot spots are stationary plumes of magma; plates moving over them build island chains.

questions.q: Which term means: the thin, rocky outer layer of Earth?
questions.explain: The term 'crust' means the thin, rocky outer layer of Earth.

questions.q: Which term means: the thick layer of hot, slowly flowing rock beneath Earth's crust?
questions.explain: The term 'mantle' means the thick layer of hot, slowly flowing rock beneath Earth's crust.

questions.q: Which term means: the theory that Earth's outer layer is divided into large plates that move slowly over time?
questions.explain: The term 'plate tectonics' means the theory that Earth's outer layer is divided into large plates that move slowly over time.

questions.q: Which term means: a crack in Earth's crust along which blocks of rock can move?
questions.explain: The term 'fault' means a crack in Earth's crust along which blocks of rock can move.

questions.q: A tectonic plate moves about 2 centimeters per year. About how far does it move in 200 years?
questions.explain: Distance = rate x time = 2 x 200 = 400 centimeters = 4 meters.

questions.q: A tectonic plate moves about 2 centimeters per year. About how far does it move in 50 years?
questions.explain: Distance = rate x time = 2 x 50 = 100 centimeters = 1 meters.

questions.q: A tectonic plate moves about 3 centimeters per year. About how far does it move in 200 years?
questions.explain: Distance = rate x time = 3 x 200 = 600 centimeters = 6 meters.

questions.q: A tectonic plate moves about 2 centimeters per year. About how far does it move in 100 years?
questions.explain: Distance = rate x time = 2 x 100 = 200 centimeters = 2 meters.

rounds.title: Earth & Space Science - Quest 1
rounds.desc: Earth's layers, tectonic plates, earthquakes, and volcanoes.

title: Earth & Space Science - Quest 2
subject: Middle School Science
description: Rock types, the rock cycle, weathering, erosion, and soil.

questions.q: Granite forms when molten rock cools slowly underground. Granite is a(n)...
questions.explain: Rocks formed from cooled magma or lava are igneous.

questions.q: Sandstone is made of sand grains pressed and cemented together. Sandstone is a(n)...
questions.explain: Compacted and cemented sediments form sedimentary rock.

questions.q: Marble forms when limestone is changed by great heat and pressure. Marble is a(n)...
questions.explain: Heat and pressure transform existing rock into metamorphic rock.

questions.q: Fossils are most commonly found in which type of rock?
questions.explain: Sediments bury organisms gently; heat in igneous and metamorphic processes usually destroys fossils.

questions.q: Water freezes in a crack in a rock, expanding and splitting the rock apart. This is an example of...
questions.explain: Ice wedging breaks rock without changing its chemistry: physical weathering.

questions.q: Acid rain slowly dissolves the surface of a limestone statue. This is an example of...
questions.explain: Acids react with the rock and change its minerals: chemical weathering.

questions.q: After rock is weathered into sediment, what process moves the sediment to a new location?
questions.explain: Erosion transports weathered material by water, wind, ice, or gravity.

questions.q: When a fast river slows down as it enters a lake, it drops its sediment. This dropping is called...
questions.explain: Deposition is the laying down of sediment in a new place.

questions.q: Soil forms from...
options: weathered rock mixed with decayed living matter (humus), air, and water
sand blown in from deserts only
questions.explain: Soil is weathered rock plus organic matter, air, and water.

questions.q: In the rock cycle, ANY rock type can become a metamorphic rock if it is...
options: buried and changed by heat and pressure
questions.explain: Heat and pressure (without full melting) create metamorphic rock from any rock type.

questions.q: To become an igneous rock, a metamorphic rock must first...
options: melt into magma, then cool and harden
questions.explain: Igneous rocks form from cooled molten rock, so melting must come first.

questions.q: Which process turns sediment into sedimentary rock?
questions.explain: Burial squeezes sediments (compaction) and minerals glue them (cementation).

questions.q: Which term means: the breaking down of rock into smaller pieces by water, wind, ice, or living things?
questions.explain: The term 'weathering' means the breaking down of rock into smaller pieces by water, wind, ice, or living things.

questions.q: What does the term 'erosion' mean?
options: the ancient supercontinent in which all of Earth's landmasses were joined together
the movement of weathered rock and soil from one place to another by water, wind, ice, or gravity
the path an object follows as it revolves around another object
an event in which one object in space casts a shadow on another object
questions.explain: 'Erosion' means the movement of weathered rock and soil from one place to another by water, wind, ice, or gravity.

questions.q: Which term means: rock that forms when melted rock cools and hardens?
questions.explain: The term 'igneous rock' means rock that forms when melted rock cools and hardens.

questions.q: Which term means: rock that forms when existing rock is changed by heat and pressure?
questions.explain: The term 'metamorphic rock' means rock that forms when existing rock is changed by heat and pressure.

questions.q: A cliff loses about 3 centimeters of rock to erosion each year. About how much rock is lost in 40 years?
questions.explain: 3 x 40 = 120 centimeters.

questions.q: Layers of sediment in a canyon wall are each about 5 meters thick. If there are 7 layers, how thick is the formation in total?
questions.explain: 5 x 7 = 35 meters.

questions.q: A sand dune migrates 8 meters per year. How far will it move in 25 years if the rate stays the same?
questions.explain: 8 x 25 = 200 meters.

questions.q: A glacier scrapes away 2 millimeters of rock surface per year. How many millimeters is that in 500 years?
questions.explain: 2 x 500 = 1000 millimeters (equal to 1 meter).

rounds.title: Earth & Space Science - Quest 2
rounds.desc: Rock types, the rock cycle, weathering, erosion, and soil.

title: Earth & Space Science - Quest 3
subject: Middle School Science
description: Rotation, revolution, seasons, Moon phases, eclipses, and tides.

questions.q: Day and night on Earth are caused by...
questions.explain: As Earth spins, different parts face the Sun, creating day and night.

questions.q: One complete rotation of Earth takes about...
questions.explain: Earth rotates once on its axis in about 24 hours.

questions.q: The seasons are caused mainly by...
options: Earth's distance from the Sun changing greatly
the tilt of Earth's axis (23.5 degrees) as it revolves around the Sun
the Sun getting hotter in summer
questions.explain: The axial tilt aims each hemisphere toward or away from the Sun during the year.

questions.q: When the Northern Hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun, it experiences...
options: equal day and night everywhere forever
summer, with longer days and more direct sunlight
questions.explain: Tilting toward the Sun brings more direct rays and longer days: summer.

questions.q: During the same month that North America has summer, Australia (Southern Hemisphere) has...
options: spring in all places at once
questions.explain: The hemispheres' seasons are opposite because of the axial tilt.

questions.q: The Moon's phases are caused by...
options: clouds in front of the Moon
Earth's shadow covering the Moon each night
the Sun lighting different parts of the Moon as the Moon orbits Earth
the Moon rotating its dark side
questions.explain: We see different amounts of the Moon's sunlit half through its monthly orbit.

questions.q: A full moon occurs when...
options: the Moon is between Earth and the Sun
the Moon is on the opposite side of Earth from the Sun, so its entire lit face is visible
questions.explain: At full moon, Earth is between the Sun and Moon, and we see the whole lit side.

questions.q: A solar eclipse happens when...
options: the Moon turns off its light
the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth and casts a shadow on Earth
the Sun passes behind the Moon permanently
Earth passes between the Sun and Moon
questions.explain: In a solar eclipse, the Moon blocks sunlight for a small area of Earth.

questions.q: A lunar eclipse happens when...
options: the Sun casts the Moon's shadow backward
the Moon enters the ocean's shadow
the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth
Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon, and Earth's shadow falls on the Moon
questions.explain: During a lunar eclipse, the Moon moves into Earth's shadow.

questions.q: Ocean tides are caused mainly by...
options: the gravitational pull of the Moon (and partly the Sun) on Earth's oceans
questions.explain: The Moon's gravity pulls ocean water into bulges, producing tides as Earth rotates.

questions.q: We always see the same side of the Moon from Earth because...
options: Earth's gravity froze the Moon's whole body solid
the Moon rotates on its axis in the same time it takes to orbit Earth
the Moon does not rotate at all
the far side is always dark
questions.explain: Synchronous rotation keeps the same face toward Earth.

questions.q: How long does Earth take to complete one revolution around the Sun?
questions.explain: One orbit takes about a year; the extra quarter day gives leap years.

questions.q: Which term means: the spinning of an object on its axis?
questions.explain: The term 'rotation' means the spinning of an object on its axis.

questions.q: Which term means: the movement of one object around another object in an orbit?
questions.explain: The term 'revolution' means the movement of one object around another object in an orbit.

questions.q: Which term means: the imaginary line passing through Earth's center and poles, around which Earth rotates?
questions.explain: The term 'axis' means the imaginary line passing through Earth's center and poles, around which Earth rotates.

questions.q: Which term means: the regular rise and fall of ocean water, caused mainly by the Moon's gravitational pull?
questions.explain: The term 'tide' means the regular rise and fall of ocean water, caused mainly by the Moon's gravitational pull.

questions.q: In 10 days, about how many times does Earth rotate on its axis?
questions.explain: Earth rotates about once per day, so about 10 times in 10 days.

questions.q: The Moon takes about 29.5 days to go through its full cycle of phases. About how many full phase cycles are there in one year (365 days)?
questions.explain: 365 / 29.5 is about 12, so roughly 12 full moons per year.

questions.q: A location on the equator travels about 40,000 kilometers in one full rotation (24 hours). About how far does it travel in 6 hours?
questions.explain: 6 hours is one quarter of a rotation: 40,000 / 4 = 10,000 kilometers.

questions.q: A high tide occurs at a beach at 6:00 AM. Tides cycle about every 12 hours. About when will the next high tide occur?
questions.explain: High tides are roughly 12 hours apart, so the next one is about 12 hours later.

rounds.title: Earth & Space Science - Quest 3
rounds.desc: Rotation, revolution, seasons, Moon phases, eclipses, and tides.

title: Earth & Space Science - Quest 4
subject: Middle School Science
description: Boss quest: the planets, comets, stars, and our place in the universe.

questions.q: Which list shows the planets in order from the Sun?
options: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Earth, Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune, Uranus
Earth, Venus, Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
Venus, Mercury, Earth, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Neptune, Uranus
questions.explain: The order is Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, then the gas and ice giants.

questions.q: Which planet is the largest in our solar system?
questions.explain: Jupiter is the largest planet, more massive than all other planets combined.

questions.q: Mars is called the Red Planet because...
options: it is covered in red plants
its surface is covered with iron-rich, rusty dust and rock
it reflects red light from a red sun
questions.explain: Iron oxide (rust) in Martian soil gives the planet its reddish color.

questions.q: Which planet is the hottest, even though it is not closest to the Sun?
options: Mercury, because it has the thickest atmosphere
Venus, because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat (runaway greenhouse effect)
questions.explain: Venus's dense CO2 atmosphere traps heat, making it hotter than Mercury.

questions.q: The asteroid belt is located between the orbits of...
questions.explain: Millions of rocky objects orbit in the belt between Mars and Jupiter.

questions.q: What keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun instead of flying off into space?
options: the Sun's gravity pulling on the planets
questions.explain: Gravity provides the inward pull that keeps planets in orbit.

questions.q: How is a star different from a planet?
options: Planets are always hotter than stars
A star produces its own light through nuclear fusion; a planet only reflects light
questions.explain: Stars generate energy by fusion; planets shine by reflected starlight.

questions.q: A comet develops a tail when it nears the Sun because...
options: the tail is made of fire like a meteor
heat vaporizes its ice, and the solar wind pushes the gas and dust away from the Sun
the comet speeds up and leaves a skid mark
questions.explain: A comet's tail of gas and dust always points away from the Sun.

questions.q: Earth is the only planet known to support life mainly because it has...
options: the strongest gravity of all planets
liquid water on its surface, a suitable temperature range, and an atmosphere with oxygen
questions.explain: Liquid water, moderate temperatures, and a breathable atmosphere make life possible.

questions.q: The four outer planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune) are mainly composed of...
options: gases and liquids (hydrogen, helium, water, ammonia, methane)
solid rock and iron like Earth
questions.explain: The outer planets are gas and ice giants, unlike the rocky inner planets.

questions.q: A light-year is a unit of...
options: distance - how far light travels in one year
questions.explain: One light-year is about 9.5 trillion kilometers - a distance, not a time.

questions.q: Our solar system is located within which galaxy?
questions.explain: The Sun is one of hundreds of billions of stars in the Milky Way.

questions.q: Which term means: the path an object follows as it revolves around another object?
questions.explain: The term 'orbit' means the path an object follows as it revolves around another object.

questions.q: Which term means: a huge system of stars, gas, and dust held together by gravity?
questions.explain: The term 'galaxy' means a huge system of stars, gas, and dust held together by gravity.

questions.q: Which term means: the Sun and all the objects that orbit it, including planets, moons, asteroids, and comets?
questions.explain: The term 'solar system' means the Sun and all the objects that orbit it, including planets, moons, asteroids, and comets.

questions.q: Which term means: an event in which one object in space casts a shadow on another object?
questions.explain: The term 'eclipse' means an event in which one object in space casts a shadow on another object.

questions.q: Sunlight takes about 500 seconds to reach Earth. Light travels 300,000 kilometers per second. About how far is Earth from the Sun?
questions.explain: Distance = speed x time = 300,000 x 500 = 150,000,000 kilometers.

questions.q: A radio signal from Earth reaches a Mars probe after 600 seconds, traveling at 300,000 kilometers per second. How far away is the probe?
questions.explain: Distance = 300,000 x 600 = 180,000,000 kilometers.

questions.q: Jupiter orbits about 5 times farther from the Sun than Earth. If Earth's distance is 1 AU (astronomical unit), Jupiter is about...
questions.explain: Jupiter's average distance is about 5 AU.

questions.q: Earth's Moon is about 384,000 kilometers away, and light travels 300,000 kilometers per second. About how long does moonlight take to reach Earth?
questions.explain: 384,000 / 300,000 is about 1.3 seconds.

rounds.title: Earth & Space Science - Quest 4
rounds.desc: Boss quest: the planets, comets, stars, and our place in the universe.

title: Weather, Climate & Review - Quest 1
subject: Middle School Science
description: Atmosphere layers, air pressure, humidity, and weather instruments.

questions.q: Which layer of the atmosphere contains nearly all of Earth's weather?
questions.explain: Weather happens in the troposphere, the layer closest to the surface.

questions.q: About what fraction of Earth's air is nitrogen?
questions.explain: Air is roughly 78 percent nitrogen, 21 percent oxygen, and 1 percent other gases.

questions.q: Oxygen makes up about what fraction of the atmosphere?
questions.explain: Oxygen is about 21 percent of the air.

questions.q: Wind blows because air moves from areas of...
options: low pressure to high pressure always
high pressure to areas of low pressure
cold ocean to cold land only
questions.explain: Air flows from high pressure toward low pressure; that moving air is wind.

questions.q: As you climb a high mountain, the air pressure...
options: decreases, because there is less air above you
becomes greater than at sea level
questions.explain: Less air overhead means less pressure at higher altitudes.

questions.q: Clouds form when water vapor in rising air...
options: cools and condenses into tiny liquid droplets around particles
questions.explain: Condensation of water vapor creates cloud droplets.

questions.q: Which instrument measures air pressure?
questions.explain: A barometer measures air pressure.

questions.q: Which instrument measures wind speed?
questions.explain: An anemometer's spinning cups measure wind speed.

questions.q: A rain gauge is used to measure...
options: the amount of precipitation that has fallen
questions.explain: Rain gauges collect and measure precipitation.

questions.q: When air reaches its dew point and cools further, what forms on grass on a clear night?
questions.explain: Water vapor condenses into liquid dew at the dew point (or frost if below freezing).

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a form of precipitation?
questions.explain: Fog is a cloud at ground level; precipitation falls from clouds to the ground.

questions.q: The ozone layer, which absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation, is found in the...
questions.explain: Ozone concentrated in the stratosphere shields life from UV radiation.

questions.q: Which term means: the layer of gases that surrounds Earth?
questions.explain: The term 'atmosphere' means the layer of gases that surrounds Earth.

questions.q: Which term means: the force exerted by the weight of the air above a surface?
questions.explain: The term 'air pressure' means the force exerted by the weight of the air above a surface.

questions.q: Which term means: the amount of water vapor present in the air?
questions.explain: The term 'humidity' means the amount of water vapor present in the air.

questions.q: Which term means: any form of water that falls from clouds to Earth's surface, such as rain, snow, sleet, or hail?
questions.explain: The term 'precipitation' means any form of water that falls from clouds to Earth's surface, such as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.

questions.q: Convert 30 degrees Celsius to degrees Fahrenheit.
questions.explain: Fahrenheit = (Celsius x 9/5) + 32, so 30 degrees Celsius = 86 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.q: Convert 77 degrees Fahrenheit to degrees Celsius.
questions.explain: Celsius = (Fahrenheit - 32) x 5/9, so 77 degrees Fahrenheit = 25 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: A weather station recorded the daily high temperature for four days. The measurements are 13, 22, 6, 3 degrees Celsius. What is the average?
questions.explain: Add the values and divide by the number of measurements (4).

questions.q: A town received 12 millimeters of rain on Monday, 8 on Tuesday, and 10 on Wednesday. What was the total rainfall?
questions.explain: 12 + 8 + 10 = 30 millimeters.

rounds.title: Weather, Climate & Review - Quest 1
rounds.desc: Atmosphere layers, air pressure, humidity, and weather instruments.

title: Weather, Climate & Review - Quest 2
subject: Middle School Science
description: Air masses, fronts, thunderstorms, tornadoes, and hurricanes.

questions.q: A cold front forms when...
options: a warm air mass slides over a cold one
a cold air mass pushes under a warm air mass, lifting it rapidly
questions.explain: Cold air wedges under warm air, often producing heavy rain or thunderstorms.

questions.q: After a cold front passes, the weather usually becomes...
questions.explain: Behind a cold front, cooler, drier air brings clearing skies.

questions.q: A warm front usually brings...
options: steady, gentle rain followed by warmer temperatures
questions.explain: Warm air sliding over cold air produces long-lasting, gentle precipitation.

questions.q: An air mass that forms over the warm, moist Gulf of Mexico is described as...
options: continental tropical - hot and dry only over land
questions.explain: Maritime tropical air masses are warm and humid.

questions.q: Air masses take on the temperature and humidity characteristics of...
options: the surface over which they form (their source region)
questions.explain: An air mass's properties come from its source region.

questions.q: A steadily FALLING barometer reading usually means...
options: stormy or unsettled weather is approaching
questions.explain: Falling pressure often signals an approaching low-pressure system and storms.

questions.q: Thunderstorms need which three ingredients?
options: ocean water, sand, and calm air
moisture, rising air (lift), and an unstable atmosphere
high pressure, sinking air, and dry air
questions.explain: Moisture, lift, and instability build the tall clouds of thunderstorms.

questions.q: During a thunderstorm, the safest place to be is...
options: in a car with the windows fully down, touching metal
in an open field lying flat with metal objects
inside a sturdy building, away from windows, water, and electrical equipment
questions.explain: Buildings protect from lightning; trees, water, and metal increase risk.

questions.q: If a tornado warning is issued, you should go to...
options: a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor, away from windows
a car and drive toward the storm
an upstairs room with large windows
questions.explain: The lowest, most interior space offers the best protection from tornado debris.

questions.q: Hurricanes form and strengthen over...
questions.explain: Warm ocean water (about 27 degrees Celsius or more) fuels hurricanes.

questions.q: Lightning is...
options: a giant electrical discharge between clouds or between a cloud and the ground
questions.explain: Lightning is static electricity discharged on a huge scale.

questions.q: Weather forecasters use Doppler radar mainly to...
options: detect precipitation and the motion of air within storms
questions.explain: Doppler radar tracks rain and wind motion inside storms, revealing rotation.

questions.q: Which term means: a large body of air that has similar temperature and humidity throughout?
questions.explain: The term 'air mass' means a large body of air that has similar temperature and humidity throughout.

questions.q: Which term means: the boundary where two air masses of different properties meet?
questions.explain: The term 'front' means the boundary where two air masses of different properties meet.

questions.q: What does the term 'barometer' mean?
options: the condition of the atmosphere at a place during a short period of time
the pattern of weather in an area over a long period of time, usually 30 years or more
a scientist who studies the atmosphere and forecasts the weather
an instrument used to measure air pressure
questions.explain: 'Barometer' means an instrument used to measure air pressure.

questions.q: What does the term 'anemometer' mean?
options: the layer of gases that surrounds Earth
an instrument used to measure wind speed
any form of water that falls from clouds to Earth's surface, such as rain, snow, sleet, or hail
the change of liquid water into water vapor (a gas)
questions.explain: 'Anemometer' means an instrument used to measure wind speed.

questions.q: A storm system travels 240 kilometers in 6 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explain: Speed = 240 / 6 = 40 kilometers per hour.

questions.q: Ahead of a warm front, the temperature is 12 degrees Celsius. Behind it, the temperature is 21 degrees Celsius. By how much did the temperature rise?
questions.explain: 21 - 12 = 9 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: A cold front drops the temperature from 24 degrees Celsius at noon to 15 degrees Celsius by 6 PM. What is the total drop?
questions.explain: 24 - 15 = 9 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: A hurricane's winds are measured at 180 kilometers per hour. A tropical storm's winds are 90 kilometers per hour. The hurricane's winds are how many times stronger by speed?
questions.explain: 180 / 90 = 2 times the wind speed.

rounds.title: Weather, Climate & Review - Quest 2
rounds.desc: Air masses, fronts, thunderstorms, tornadoes, and hurricanes.

title: Weather, Climate & Review - Quest 3
subject: Middle School Science
description: Climate patterns, the greenhouse effect, and human-caused climate change.

questions.q: Which statement describes CLIMATE rather than weather?
options: 'It rained for an hour this afternoon'
'Summers in this desert region are usually hot and dry'
questions.explain: Climate is the long-term pattern; the others are short-term conditions.

questions.q: Which factor has the GREATEST influence on an area's climate?
options: latitude - how far the area is from the equator
questions.explain: Latitude determines how directly sunlight strikes, shaping temperature patterns.

questions.q: Places at high altitude (like mountain towns) usually have ______ climates than nearby lowlands at the same latitude.
questions.explain: Temperature generally decreases with altitude.

questions.q: The greenhouse effect is necessary for life on Earth because without it, Earth would...
options: be too cold for liquid water in most places
questions.explain: Natural greenhouse gases keep Earth about 33 degrees Celsius warmer than it would otherwise be.

questions.q: Which human activity most directly increases carbon dioxide in the atmosphere?
options: burning fossil fuels such as coal, oil, and natural gas
questions.explain: Combustion of fossil fuels releases stored carbon as CO2.

questions.q: Which of these is evidence that Earth's climate is warming?
options: one town had a cold day last winter
glaciers and ice sheets are shrinking, and global sea level is rising
questions.explain: Long-term records of ice loss and sea-level rise show warming; single weather events do not prove or disprove climate trends.

questions.q: As extra greenhouse gases trap more heat, one expected effect is...
options: more frequent and intense heat waves and changes in precipitation patterns
an immediate new ice age everywhere
questions.explain: Warming shifts weather patterns, intensifying heat and altering rainfall.

questions.q: Which action would most reduce a school's carbon footprint?
options: using energy-efficient lighting and reducing electricity waste
questions.explain: Using less fossil-fuel energy cuts CO2 emissions.

questions.q: Why are scientists confident that recent warming is mostly caused by humans?
options: Because the Sun has doubled in brightness
Because every scientist voted on it
Climate models and measurements show the warming matches the rise in human-produced greenhouse gases, and natural factors alone cannot explain it
questions.explain: Observed warming patterns fit greenhouse-gas increases, not natural causes like solar changes.

questions.q: Planting trees helps slow climate change because trees...
options: absorb carbon dioxide from the air during photosynthesis
cool the planet by their shade alone on a global scale
block all sunlight to the ground
produce carbon dioxide at night only
questions.explain: Photosynthesis removes CO2 and stores carbon in wood and soil.

questions.q: Which gas is a greenhouse gas produced by burning fuels AND by livestock and rice farming?
questions.explain: Methane comes from fossil fuels, livestock digestion, and flooded rice fields.

questions.q: Ice at the poles melting into the ocean causes sea level to rise. A second cause of sea-level rise is...
options: thermal expansion - seawater expands as it warms
questions.explain: Warming water takes up more space, raising sea level along with meltwater.

questions.q: Which term means: the pattern of weather in an area over a long period of time, usually 30 years or more?
questions.explain: The term 'climate' means the pattern of weather in an area over a long period of time, usually 30 years or more.

questions.q: What does the term 'weather' mean?
options: the condition of the atmosphere at a place during a short period of time
a large body of air that has similar temperature and humidity throughout
the increase in Earth's average surface temperature over time
the layer of gases that surrounds Earth
questions.explain: 'Weather' means the condition of the atmosphere at a place during a short period of time.

questions.q: Which term means: the trapping of heat in the atmosphere by certain gases, which keeps Earth's surface warm?
questions.explain: The term 'greenhouse effect' means the trapping of heat in the atmosphere by certain gases, which keeps Earth's surface warm.

questions.q: Which term means: energy sources formed from the remains of ancient organisms, such as coal, oil, and natural gas?
questions.explain: The term 'fossil fuels' means energy sources formed from the remains of ancient organisms, such as coal, oil, and natural gas.

questions.q: Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere has risen from about 280 parts per million (pre-industrial) to about 420 parts per million today. By about what percent did it increase?
questions.explain: Increase = 420 - 280 = 140; 140 / 280 = 0.5, about 50 percent.

questions.q: Sea level rises about 3 millimeters per year. At this rate, how much will it rise in 10 years?
questions.explain: 3 x 10 = 30 millimeters = 3 centimeters.

questions.q: A city's average summer temperature was 26 degrees Celsius in 1990 and 28 degrees Celsius in 2020. What was the increase over the 30 years?
questions.explain: 28 - 26 = 2 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: A glacier retreats 15 meters each year. How far will it retreat in 20 years at this rate?
questions.explain: 15 x 20 = 300 meters.

rounds.title: Weather, Climate & Review - Quest 3
rounds.desc: Climate patterns, the greenhouse effect, and human-caused climate change.

title: Weather, Climate & Review - Quest 4
subject: Middle School Science
description: Boss quest: grand review of the whole year - science skills, cells, body, ecosystems, matter, forces, energy, and Earth science.

questions.q: A student writes: 'If bean seeds receive more water, then they will sprout faster.' This statement is a(n)...
questions.explain: It is a testable if-then prediction: a hypothesis.

questions.q: A cell that must swim long distances needs a large amount of energy. Which organelle would it need in large numbers?
questions.explain: Mitochondria release the energy such a cell needs for movement.

questions.q: Which body system removes carbon dioxide from the blood and releases it from the body?
questions.explain: The lungs exhale carbon dioxide collected by the blood.

questions.q: In the food chain algae -> krill -> penguin -> leopard seal, the penguin is a...
questions.explain: Krill (primary consumer) are eaten by penguins, making penguins secondary consumers.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a chemical change?
options: food being broken down by stomach acid and enzymes
questions.explain: Digestion chemically transforms food into new substances.

questions.q: A 10-newton force pulls a box east and a 10-newton force pulls it west at the same time. What is the net force on the box?
questions.explain: Equal forces in opposite directions cancel: net force is zero.

questions.q: Which moving object has more kinetic energy? Object A: mass 1000 kilograms, speed 10 meters per second. Object B: mass 200 kilograms, speed 20 meters per second.
Which daily event is a direct result of Earth's rotation?
options: the cycle of day and night
the yearly path of constellations only
questions.explain: Rotation causes day and night; seasons come from tilt plus revolution.

questions.q: A barometer at school shows pressure dropping steadily all morning. What weather is most likely coming?
questions.explain: Falling pressure usually means an approaching low-pressure system and storms.

questions.q: If acid is spilled on a lab bench, what should you do FIRST?
options: wipe it up with your bare hand
pour another chemical on it to neutralize it by guessing
leave it for the next class
questions.explain: The teacher must be told at once so the spill can be handled safely.

questions.q: Which process releases energy from glucose in BOTH plant and animal cells?
questions.explain: All living cells respire to release energy; only some cells photosynthesize.

questions.q: Which group of organisms returns nutrients from dead plants and animals to the soil?
options: decomposers such as bacteria and fungi
questions.explain: Decomposers break down dead matter and recycle its nutrients.

questions.q: An atom has an atomic number of 13. How many protons does it contain?
questions.explain: Atomic number equals the number of protons.

questions.q: A runner covers 400 meters in 50 seconds. What is the runner's average speed?
questions.explain: Speed = 400 / 50 = 8 meters per second.

questions.q: The warmth of sunlight on your skin reached you by...
questions.explain: Sunlight's energy crosses space by radiation.

questions.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet because of its iron-rich, rusty surface?
questions.explain: Mars appears red due to iron oxide dust.

questions.q: While you sprint, your breathing rate rises mainly because your muscle cells need more...
options: oxygen to release energy from glucose
questions.explain: Working muscles respire faster, demanding more oxygen and producing more CO2.

questions.q: If the frequency of a sound wave increases, the sound's pitch will...
questions.explain: Higher frequency means higher pitch.

questions.q: A bathroom mirror fogs up during a hot shower because water vapor undergoes...
options: condensation on the cooler mirror surface
questions.explain: Water vapor condenses into liquid droplets on the cool mirror.

questions.q: Fossils are most often preserved in which type of rock?
questions.explain: Sedimentary layers bury organisms under conditions that can preserve fossils.

title: Year Quest: Story Parts: Who, Where & What Happens - Quest 1
subject: Kids Reading
description: Read mini stories and find who, where, and what happens. Quest 1 of 4 in this unit.

questions.q: Zoe lost her red mitten at the park. She looked under the bench. She found it there and cheered. Where did Zoe lose her mitten?
questions.explain: The story says Zoe was at the park.

questions.q: Kai saw snow falling outside. He put on his boots and coat and ran into his yard. He made a snowman with a carrot nose. What did Kai make?
questions.explain: The story says Kai made a snowman.

questions.q: Ella drew a picture of her house. She used red for the roof. She gave the picture to her mom. What color did Ella use for the roof?
questions.explain: The story says Ella used red for the roof.

questions.q: Ruby found a shiny shell at the beach. She held it up to her ear. She heard a soft sound, like the sea. Where did Ruby find the shell?
options: in the sand box at home
questions.explain: The story says Ruby was at the beach.

questions.q: A little bird sat in a tree by the school. It sang a happy song. Two kids stopped to listen. Where was the bird sitting?
questions.explain: The story says the bird sat in a tree.

questions.q: Zoe lost her red mitten at the park. She looked under the bench. She found it there and cheered. What did Zoe find under the bench?
questions.explain: The story says Zoe found her red mitten under the bench.

questions.q: Lily found a lost puppy near her house. She gave it a bowl of water. The happy puppy wagged its tail. Who found a lost puppy?
questions.explain: The story says Lily found the puppy.

questions.q: Tom picked apples at the farm. He filled a big basket to the top. Then he ate one crisp apple. What did Tom put in the basket?
questions.explain: The story says Tom filled the basket with apples.

questions.q: Kai saw snow falling outside. He put on his boots and coat and ran into his yard. He made a snowman with a carrot nose. Where did Kai make the snowman?
questions.explain: The story says Kai ran into his yard.

options: It flew high in the sky.
It got stuck in a tree.
questions.explain: The story says the kite flew high in the sky.

questions.q: Mrs. Fox read a story to her class at school. The story was about a brave little mouse. The class clapped at the end. Where was the class?
questions.explain: The story says the class was at school.

questions.explain: The story says Leo liked to nap in the warm sun.

questions.explain: The story says Sam built the sand castle.

questions.explain: The story says the two kids stopped to listen.

questions.explain: The story says Mia planted the seed in her garden.

questions.explain: The story says Tom picked the apples.

questions.explain: The story says Nora pulled up the carrots in the fall.

title: Year Quest: Plants & How They Grow - Quest 1
subject: Kids Science
description: Roots, stems, leaves, and flowers: learn the parts of a plant and the job each one does.

questions.q: Which part of a plant has this job: take in water and minerals from the soil?
questions.explain: Each plant part has a job. The roots take in water and minerals from the soil.

questions.q: What is the job of the roots?
options: Take in water and minerals from the soil
Makes seeds so new plants can grow
Use sunlight to make food for the plant
Holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves
questions.explain: The roots take in water and minerals from the soil.

questions.q: Which part of a plant has this job: holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves?
questions.explain: Each plant part has a job. The stem holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves.

questions.q: What is the job of the stem?
options: Makes seeds so new plants can grow
Can grow into a new plant
Holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves
questions.explain: The stem holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves.

questions.q: Which part of a plant has this job: use sunlight to make food for the plant?
questions.explain: Each plant part has a job. The leaves use sunlight to make food for the plant.

questions.q: What is the job of the leaves?
options: Use sunlight to make food for the plant
Holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves
Take in water and minerals from the soil
questions.explain: The leaves use sunlight to make food for the plant.

questions.q: Which part of a plant has this job: makes seeds so new plants can grow?
questions.explain: Each plant part has a job. The flower makes seeds so new plants can grow.

questions.q: What is the job of the flower?
options: Makes seeds so new plants can grow
Can grow into a new plant
Holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves
Use sunlight to make food for the plant
questions.explain: The flower makes seeds so new plants can grow.

questions.q: Which part of a plant has this job: can grow into a new plant?
questions.explain: Each plant part has a job. A seed can grow into a new plant.

questions.q: What is the job of a seed?
options: Makes seeds so new plants can grow
Take in water and minerals from the soil
Can grow into a new plant
questions.explain: A seed can grow into a new plant.

questions.q: Which part of a plant has this job: holds and protects the seeds?
questions.explain: Each plant part has a job. The fruit holds and protects the seeds.

questions.q: What is the job of the fruit?
options: Take in water and minerals from the soil
Use sunlight to make food for the plant
Holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves
questions.explain: The fruit holds and protects the seeds.

questions.q: Which part of a plant grows mostly under the ground?
questions.explain: Roots grow underground and take in water from the soil.

questions.q: Bees visit this part of the plant and help it make seeds. Which part is it?
questions.explain: Bees help flowers by moving pollen, and flowers make seeds.

questions.q: Which part of a carrot plant do people eat?
questions.explain: A carrot is the root of the carrot plant.

questions.q: A plant part is wide, flat, and green, and it catches sunlight. Which part is it?
questions.explain: Leaves are usually wide and green so they can catch sunlight.

questions.q: After a flower is pollinated, what can grow inside the plant?
questions.explain: Flowers make seeds so new plants can grow.

questions.q: Which part carries water from the roots up to the leaves?
questions.explain: The stem carries water from the roots to the rest of the plant.

questions.q: A tiny new plant is growing inside something small and hard. What is it growing inside?
questions.explain: A seed holds a tiny new plant and food for it to start growing.

questions.q: An apple is which part of the apple tree?
questions.explain: An apple is a fruit. It holds the apple tree's seeds.

title: Year Quest: Plants & How They Grow - Quest 3
subject: Kids Science
description: From seed to sprout to flower and back to seeds: follow the plant life cycle.

questions.q: What is the first stage in the life of most plants?
questions.explain: Most plants begin life as a seed.

questions.q: When a seed starts to grow, it is said to...
questions.explain: When a seed starts to grow, it sprouts. This is called germination.

questions.q: What part of a sprouting seed grows first?
questions.explain: The root grows first so the young plant can take in water.

questions.q: What do we call a young plant that has just sprouted?
questions.explain: A young plant is called a seedling.

questions.q: Put these in order: seed, adult plant with flowers, sprout, seedling.
options: Adult plant with flowers, seed, sprout, seedling
Seed, seedling, sprout, adult plant with flowers
Sprout, seed, adult plant with flowers, seedling
Seed, sprout, seedling, adult plant with flowers
questions.explain: A plant grows from seed to sprout to seedling to adult.

questions.q: How do dandelion seeds travel to new places?
options: They are blown by the wind
questions.explain: Dandelion seeds are light and fluffy, so the wind carries them.

questions.q: A squirrel buries an acorn and forgets it. What may happen in spring?
options: The acorn may sprout into an oak tree
The acorn turns into a squirrel
questions.explain: Animals help spread seeds. A buried acorn can sprout into an oak tree.

questions.q: Why do many plants make fruits around their seeds?
options: Fruit keeps seeds in the dark
Animals eat the fruit and spread the seeds
questions.explain: Animals eat fruit and drop or pass the seeds in new places, spreading them.

questions.q: What do bees carry from flower to flower that helps plants make seeds?
questions.explain: Bees carry pollen between flowers, which helps flowers make seeds.

questions.q: A sunflower makes many seeds in the center of its flower. What are those seeds for?
questions.explain: Seeds can grow into new plants.

questions.q: What does a seed hold inside it?
options: A tiny new plant and food for it
questions.explain: A seed holds a tiny new plant plus stored food to help it start growing.

questions.q: Which conditions help most seeds sprout?
questions.explain: Most seeds need water, air, and warmth to sprout.

questions.q: After a seedling grows more leaves, what can it do better?
options: Make more of its own food using sunlight
questions.explain: More leaves catch more sunlight, so the plant can make more food.

questions.q: A bean seed is planted and kept wet. After a few days, a small root and shoot appear. The seed has...
questions.explain: When a seed begins to grow, we say it has sprouted.

questions.q: Which plant part makes the seeds that start the cycle again?
questions.explain: Flowers make seeds, and the seeds can start new plants.

questions.q: Why is the life of a plant called a cycle?
options: It repeats: seeds grow into plants that make new seeds
Plants only grow in round pots
questions.explain: A cycle repeats. Seeds become plants, and those plants make new seeds.

questions.q: Tomato seeds are inside the tomato. If you plant them in soil and water them, they can...
questions.explain: Seeds from a tomato can grow into new tomato plants.

questions.q: What is one way seeds are spread by water?
options: They float to a new place
questions.explain: Some seeds float on water and land in new places where they can grow.

questions.q: A maple seed has a wing-like shape. How does that help it?
options: The wind can carry it away from the tree
It can fly like a bird
questions.explain: Wing-shaped seeds spin in the air and are carried by the wind.

questions.q: What happens to many adult plants after they make seeds?
options: The cycle can start again with the new seeds
The seeds turn into soil at once
questions.explain: New seeds can grow into new plants, so the cycle continues.

questions.q: A doctor checks the brain of a patient. What job is the doctor checking?
options: Controls the body and lets you think and remember
Give the body shape and support
Pull on bones to help the body move
questions.explain: The brain controls the body and lets you think and remember.

questions.q: A doctor checks the stomach of a patient. What job is the doctor checking?
options: Pull on bones to help the body move
Chop and chew food into small pieces
questions.explain: The stomach breaks down food you eat.

questions.q: A doctor checks the bones of a patient. What job is the doctor checking?
options: Chop and chew food into small pieces
Pumps blood all around the body
Give the body shape and support
questions.explain: The bones give the body shape and support.

questions.q: A doctor checks the muscles of a patient. What job is the doctor checking?
options: Pull on bones to help the body move
Chop and chew food into small pieces
Take in air when you breathe
Pumps blood all around the body
questions.explain: The muscles pull on bones to help the body move.

questions.q: Why does your heart beat faster when you play tag?
options: Your heart is scared of tag
Your muscles need more blood and air while you move
questions.explain: During exercise the heart pumps faster to send more blood and air to the muscles.

questions.q: Which body part works like a control center, sending messages to the rest of the body?
questions.explain: The brain controls the body and sends and receives messages.

questions.q: What do muscles need from the blood to keep working?
questions.explain: Blood carries oxygen and food energy to the muscles.

questions.q: Which sense would warn you that soup is too hot before you take a big bite?
questions.explain: Touch in your mouth and taste buds warn you about heat and flavor.

questions.q: Why do people wear helmets when riding bikes?
options: To protect the head and brain from injury
questions.explain: A helmet protects the skull and the brain inside it.

questions.q: Your stomach growls when you are hungry. What is your stomach's main job?
questions.explain: The stomach breaks down food so the body can use it.

questions.q: Which pair is matched correctly?
questions.explain: The lungs are the organs for breathing air.

questions.q: What is the largest sense organ of the body?
questions.explain: Skin is the body's largest organ, and it gives the sense of touch.

rounds.title: Year Quest: The Human Body & Senses - Quest 4

title: Year Quest: Weather & Seasons - Quest 1
subject: Kids Science
description: Thermometers, rain gauges, and storm clouds: learn how we observe and describe weather.

questions.q: What does a thermometer measure or show?
options: How hot or cold the air is
The direction the wind comes from
Which way the wind is blowing and how strong it is
questions.explain: A thermometer shows how hot or cold the air is.

questions.q: Which tool would you use to find how hot or cold the air is?
questions.explain: A thermometer is the tool for that job.

questions.q: What does a rain gauge measure or show?
options: The direction the wind comes from
How hot or cold the air is
Which way the wind is blowing and how strong it is
questions.explain: A rain gauge shows how much rain has fallen.

questions.q: Which tool would you use to find how much rain has fallen?
questions.explain: A rain gauge is the tool for that job.

questions.q: What does a windsock measure or show?
options: Which way the wind is blowing and how strong it is
The direction the wind comes from
How hot or cold the air is
questions.explain: A windsock shows which way the wind is blowing and how strong it is.

questions.q: Which tool would you use to find which way the wind is blowing and how strong it is?
questions.explain: A windsock is the tool for that job.

questions.q: What does a weather vane measure or show?
options: How hot or cold the air is
Which way the wind is blowing and how strong it is
The direction the wind comes from
questions.explain: A weather vane shows the direction the wind comes from.

questions.q: Which tool would you use to find the direction the wind comes from?
questions.explain: A weather vane is the tool for that job.

questions.q: Dark clouds gather and rain begins to fall. How would you describe the weather?
questions.explain: Weather words describe what the air and sky are like outside.

questions.q: The temperature is 30 degrees and snow covers the ground. The weather is...
questions.explain: Temperature and what falls from the sky describe the weather.

questions.q: Which of these is a kind of weather?
questions.explain: Weather is what the air outside is like, such as storms, sun, or snow.

questions.q: What does the word weather mean?
options: What the air and sky are like outside at a time and place
questions.explain: Weather describes the air outside: temperature, wind, clouds, and rain or snow.

questions.q: A weather reporter says tomorrow will be windy. What will the air do tomorrow?
questions.explain: Wind is moving air. A windy day means the air is moving fast.

questions.q: Which tool tells how hot or cold something is?
questions.explain: A thermometer measures temperature, how hot or cold something is.

questions.q: Fog is...
options: tiny water drops floating in the air near the ground
questions.explain: Fog is a cloud of tiny water drops that forms near the ground.

questions.q: If the sky is clear and the sun is shining, the weather is...
questions.explain: A clear sky with sunshine means sunny weather.

questions.q: Which weather is most dangerous to be outside in?
questions.explain: Lightning makes thunderstorms dangerous. People should go inside during storms.

questions.q: What falls from clouds when the air is very cold?
questions.explain: When the air is very cold, water in clouds can fall as snow.

questions.q: A puddle is gone after a sunny afternoon. Where did the water go?
options: It sank to the center of Earth
questions.explain: The sun warmed the puddle and the water evaporated, turning into vapor in the air.

questions.q: Which of these would a weather scientist watch?
questions.explain: Weather scientists study clouds, wind, temperature, and rain.

rounds.title: Year Quest: Weather & Seasons - Quest 1
rounds.desc: Thermometers, rain gauges, and storm clouds: learn how we observe and describe weather.

title: Year Quest: Weather & Seasons - Quest 2
subject: Kids Science
description: Spring, summer, fall, winter: discover what makes each season special and how they repeat.

questions.q: In which season do flowers bloom, baby animals are born, and the air gets warmer?
questions.explain: In spring, flowers bloom, baby animals are born, and the air gets warmer.

questions.q: Which season is described here: flowers bloom, baby animals are born, and the air gets warmer?
questions.explain: That is spring, when flowers bloom, baby animals are born, and the air gets warmer.

questions.q: In which season do the days are long and the weather is hottest?
questions.explain: In summer, the days are long and the weather is hottest.

questions.q: Which season is described here: the days are long and the weather is hottest?
questions.explain: That is summer, when the days are long and the weather is hottest.

questions.q: In which season do leaves change color and drop from many trees?
questions.explain: In fall (autumn), leaves change color and drop from many trees.

questions.q: Which season is described here: leaves change color and drop from many trees?
questions.explain: That is fall (autumn), when leaves change color and drop from many trees.

questions.q: In which season do the weather is coldest and some places get snow?
questions.explain: In winter, the weather is coldest and some places get snow.

questions.q: Which season is described here: the weather is coldest and some places get snow?
questions.explain: That is winter, when the weather is coldest and some places get snow.

questions.q: Which season comes right after summer?
questions.explain: The seasons go in order: spring, summer, fall, winter, then spring again.

questions.q: Which season comes right before spring?
questions.explain: Winter is the season before spring.

questions.q: In what order do the four seasons repeat?
questions.explain: The seasons repeat in the same order every year.

questions.q: Which clothes are best for a hot summer day?
questions.explain: Light clothes help you stay cool in summer heat.

questions.q: Which activity fits a snowy winter day?
questions.explain: Snow in winter is good for building snowmen and sledding.

questions.q: In fall, many trees...
questions.explain: In fall, the leaves of many trees change color and drop.

questions.q: Why are summer days longer than winter days in the United States?
options: Earth is tilted, so the Northern Hemisphere gets more direct sunlight and longer days in summer
The sun moves closer in summer
questions.explain: Earth's tilt gives one part of the planet longer, warmer days in its summer.

questions.q: Farmers often plant seeds in which season?
questions.explain: Spring warmth and rain help seeds sprout, so farmers plant in spring.

questions.q: Which season would you most likely see baby birds in nests?
questions.explain: Many birds lay eggs and raise babies in spring.

questions.q: Apples are often picked ripe in which season?
questions.explain: Many apple orchards harvest ripe apples in the fall.

questions.q: What happens to many animals in winter?
options: All animals fly to the beach
Some hibernate and some grow thicker fur
questions.explain: Animals adapt to winter cold by hibernating, migrating, or growing thick fur.

questions.q: Which season has the shortest, coldest days in the United States?
questions.explain: Winter days are the shortest and coldest of the year.

rounds.title: Year Quest: Weather & Seasons - Quest 2
rounds.desc: Spring, summer, fall, winter: discover what makes each season special and how they repeat.

title: Year Quest: Weather & Seasons - Quest 3
subject: Kids Science
description: Evaporation, clouds, and rain: follow a drop of water on its endless cycle.

questions.q: Where does rain come from?
options: Water drops in clouds fall when they get heavy
Wind shakes rain out of trees
questions.explain: Clouds hold tiny water drops. When drops join and get heavy, they fall as rain.

questions.q: What is the water cycle?
options: Water flows in a circle-shaped river
Water moves from the ground to the air and back again as rain or snow
questions.explain: In the water cycle, water evaporates, forms clouds, falls as rain or snow, and collects again.

questions.q: What does the sun do in the water cycle?
options: It heats water so it evaporates into the air
questions.explain: Sunlight heats water in puddles, lakes, and oceans, and some of it evaporates.

questions.q: When water vapor cools high in the sky, it forms...
questions.explain: Cooled water vapor joins into tiny drops that make clouds.

questions.q: What is evaporation?
options: When liquid water changes into a gas and goes into the air
questions.explain: Evaporation is liquid water changing into water vapor, a gas.

questions.q: Wet clothes dry on a line because...
options: the clothes squeeze out all water at once
questions.explain: Water in wet clothes evaporates into the air, leaving the clothes dry.

questions.q: Drops of water appear on the outside of a cold glass. Where did they come from?
options: Water vapor in the air cooled and turned back into liquid on the glass
questions.explain: This is condensation: water vapor in the air changes into liquid on a cold surface.

questions.q: After rain, water collects in lakes, rivers, and puddles. Then the sun shines. What happens next in the cycle?
options: Some water evaporates and the cycle continues
questions.explain: The water cycle keeps repeating: collect, evaporate, condense, fall.

questions.q: Snow melts on a warm spring day. The meltwater will most likely...
options: flow into streams and soil, and some will evaporate
questions.explain: Melted snow joins streams and soil, and some evaporates back into the air.

questions.q: Which list shows the water cycle in a good order?
options: Water collects, rain falls, clouds form, sun cools
Clouds form, water collects, rain falls, evaporation stops
Evaporation, clouds form, rain falls, water collects
Rain falls, evaporation, water collects, clouds form
questions.explain: Water evaporates, forms clouds, falls as rain, and collects, then it repeats.

questions.q: Why does a bathroom mirror fog up during a hot shower?
options: The shower sprays the mirror directly only
Water vapor in the warm air condenses on the cooler mirror
questions.explain: Warm air holds water vapor. On a cooler mirror, the vapor condenses into tiny drops.

questions.q: Clouds are made of...
options: tiny water drops or ice crystals
questions.explain: Clouds are made of tiny water drops or ice crystals floating in the air.

questions.q: What do we call water that falls from clouds?
questions.explain: Precipitation is the science word for water falling from clouds.

questions.q: A lake slowly gets smaller during a hot, dry summer. Why?
options: More water evaporates than falls as rain
questions.explain: In hot, dry weather, evaporation takes water out of a lake faster than rain adds it.

questions.q: Morning dew on grass comes from...
options: water vapor in the air condensing on cool grass
questions.explain: At night, cool grass makes water vapor in the air condense into dew drops.

questions.q: If there were no sun, what would happen to the water cycle?
options: Evaporation would mostly stop and the cycle would slow down
questions.explain: The sun's heat powers evaporation, which drives the water cycle.

questions.q: Which is an example of condensation?
options: Fog forming on a cool morning
questions.explain: Fog is water vapor condensing into tiny drops in cool air.

questions.q: Which is an example of evaporation?
options: A wet sidewalk drying after a storm
questions.explain: A drying sidewalk shows water evaporating into the air.

questions.q: Rain falls on a mountain. Much of it flows downhill into a river because of...
questions.explain: Gravity pulls rainwater downhill into streams and rivers.

questions.q: Why is the water cycle important for farms?
options: It makes the sun shine longer
It brings rain that waters the crops
questions.explain: Rain from the water cycle gives crops the water they need.

rounds.title: Year Quest: Weather & Seasons - Quest 3
rounds.desc: Evaporation, clouds, and rain: follow a drop of water on its endless cycle.

subject: Kids Science

questions.q: Thunder booms and lightning flashes. What is the safest thing to do?
options: Fly a kite in the field
Go inside a building and stay away from windows
questions.explain: During thunderstorms, go indoors. Lightning can strike trees, water, and open fields.

questions.q: Which is the safest place during a tornado?
options: A small inside room or basement away from windows
questions.explain: During a tornado, shelter in a basement or a small inside room away from windows.

questions.q: On a very sunny day at the beach, how can you protect your skin?
options: Use sunscreen, wear a hat, and take shade breaks
Stay in the sun all day
Use baby oil to tan faster
questions.explain: Sunscreen, hats, and shade protect skin from the sun's strong rays.

questions.q: It is a freezing winter morning. Which outfit is safest and warmest?
options: A warm coat, hat, gloves, and boots
questions.explain: Layers, a coat, hat, and gloves protect you in freezing weather.

questions.q: Flood water covers a street. What should you do?
options: Stay away and never walk or play in flood water
questions.explain: Flood water can be deep and dangerous. Never walk or play in it.

questions.q: The weather report warns of a hot day of 100 degrees. What is a smart plan?
options: Drink water, rest in the shade, and play outside in cooler hours
questions.explain: On very hot days, drink water and avoid the strongest heat.

questions.q: Which sign warns that a thunderstorm may be coming?
options: Dark storm clouds and distant thunder
questions.explain: Dark clouds, wind, and thunder are signs of a coming storm.

questions.q: Why should you come inside when you see lightning, even before rain starts?
options: Lightning can strike before the rain arrives
questions.explain: Lightning can strike miles ahead of a storm, so go inside when you see it.

questions.q: What should you do with outdoor toys when a big storm is coming?
options: Bring them inside so the wind cannot blow them away
questions.explain: Strong storm winds can blow loose objects around, so bring them inside.

questions.q: Which season needs sunscreen most often in the United States?
questions.explain: Summer sunlight is strongest, so sunscreen matters most then.

questions.q: Review: in which season do the days are long and the weather is hottest?
questions.explain: In summer, the days are long and the weather is hottest.

questions.q: Review: which season is described here: the days are long and the weather is hottest?
questions.explain: That is summer, when the days are long and the weather is hottest.

questions.q: Review: in which season do leaves change color and drop from many trees?

questions.q: Review: which season is described here: leaves change color and drop from many trees?
questions.explain: That is fall (autumn), when leaves change color and drop from many trees.

questions.q: Review: in which season do the weather is coldest and some places get snow?
questions.explain: In winter, the weather is coldest and some places get snow.

questions.q: Review: what is the water cycle?
options: Water moves from the ground to the air and back again as rain or snow
Water flows in a circle-shaped river

questions.q: Review: what does the sun do in the water cycle?
options: It heats water so it evaporates into the air

questions.q: Review: when water vapor cools high in the sky, it forms...

questions.q: Review: what is evaporation?
options: When liquid water changes into a gas and goes into the air
questions.explain: Evaporation is liquid water changing into water vapor, a gas.

questions.q: Review: wet clothes dry on a line because...
options: the clothes squeeze out all water at once
questions.explain: Water in wet clothes evaporates into the air, leaving the clothes dry.

title: Year Quest: Earth, Sun & Moon - Quest 1
subject: Kids Science
description: Our spinning planet: learn how Earth's rotation gives us day and night.

questions.q: Earth is a...
questions.explain: Earth is a planet. It moves around the Sun.

questions.q: Why do we have day and night?
options: Earth spins (rotates), so different sides face the Sun
The Sun goes to sleep at night
The Moon covers the Sun all night
questions.explain: Earth rotates once each day. The side facing the Sun has daytime.

questions.q: When your side of Earth faces the Sun, it is...
questions.explain: The side of Earth facing the Sun is lit up: it is daytime there.

questions.q: When your side of Earth faces away from the Sun, it is...
questions.explain: The side of Earth facing away from the Sun is dark: it is nighttime there.

questions.q: How long does Earth take to spin around once?
questions.explain: Earth makes one full rotation in about 24 hours, giving us day and night.

questions.q: How long does Earth take to travel all the way around the Sun?
questions.explain: Earth orbits the Sun once each year.

questions.q: What is the path Earth follows around the Sun called?
questions.explain: An orbit is the path a planet follows around the Sun.

questions.q: Most of Earth's surface is covered by...
questions.explain: Oceans cover most of Earth's surface.

questions.q: The great pieces of land on Earth are called...
questions.explain: Earth has seven large pieces of land called continents.

questions.q: What force keeps your feet on the ground and pulls things down?
questions.explain: Gravity is the force that pulls objects toward Earth.

questions.q: In a science model, a globe spins in front of a flashlight. The flashlight stands for...
questions.explain: In the model, the flashlight's light stands for sunlight from the Sun.

questions.q: In that globe and flashlight model, the lit half of the globe shows...
options: where it is daytime on Earth
questions.explain: The half of Earth lit by the Sun is having daytime.

questions.q: As the globe keeps spinning, a spot moves from the lit half to the dark half. On Earth, that spot would be having...
questions.explain: As Earth rotates, places move from sunlight into darkness at sunset.

questions.q: Why does the Sun look like it moves across the sky during the day?
options: Because the Sun travels around Earth each day
questions.explain: Earth's rotation makes the Sun appear to move across the sky.

questions.q: How many moons does Earth have?
questions.explain: Earth has just one moon.

questions.q: Earth is the only planet known to...
questions.explain: Earth is the only planet known to have life.

questions.q: What do we call a full turn of Earth on its axis?
questions.explain: One full spin of Earth is called a rotation.

questions.q: What do we call Earth's trip around the Sun?
questions.explain: Earth's trip around the Sun is its revolution, and it takes one year.

questions.q: If Earth did not spin at all, what would happen?
options: One side would always be day and the other always night
questions.explain: Earth's spinning gives every place a cycle of day and night.

questions.q: Which is TRUE about Earth?
options: It sits still while the Sun orbits it
It spins on an imaginary line called its axis
It is flat like a plate
questions.explain: Earth rotates on its axis, an imaginary line through its poles.

rounds.title: Year Quest: Earth, Sun & Moon - Quest 1
