title: Year Quest: Earth, Sun & Moon - Quest 2
subject: Kids Science
description: The Sun is a star that gives us light and heat. Study its path and your changing shadow.

questions.q: The Sun is a...
questions.explain: The Sun is a star, a huge ball of hot, glowing gas.

questions.q: Why does the Sun look bigger than other stars?
options: It is much closer to Earth
It is the biggest star of all
It is inside our solar system alone
questions.explain: The Sun looks big because it is our closest star. Other stars are far, far away.

questions.q: What two things does the Sun give Earth?
questions.explain: The Sun gives Earth light and heat, which living things need.

questions.q: The Sun rises in the...
questions.explain: The Sun appears to rise in the east and set in the west because Earth spins.

questions.q: The Sun sets in the...
questions.explain: The Sun appears to set in the west.

questions.q: When is the Sun highest in the sky?
options: Around the middle of the day (noon)
questions.explain: The Sun reaches its highest point around noon.

questions.q: Your shadow is longest...
options: in the early morning and late afternoon
questions.explain: When the Sun is low, shadows are long. At noon, shadows are short.

questions.q: At noon on a sunny day, your shadow is...
options: gone to the other side of Earth
questions.explain: When the Sun is high overhead, shadows are short.

questions.q: A shadow forms when...
questions.explain: Shadows form where an object blocks light from reaching a surface.

questions.q: On which side of a tree is its shadow in the morning, when the Sun is in the east?
options: There is no shadow in the morning
On the west side, away from the Sun
On the east side, toward the Sun
questions.explain: Shadows point away from the light, so a morning shadow falls to the west.

questions.q: Why should you never look straight at the Sun?
options: Its strong light can hurt your eyes
It is too far to see
questions.explain: The Sun's light is so strong it can damage eyes. Never stare at it.

questions.q: How do plants use sunlight?
questions.explain: Plants use sunlight, air, and water to make food.

questions.q: What would happen to Earth without the Sun's heat?
options: Earth would be freezing cold and dark
questions.explain: The Sun's heat keeps Earth warm enough for living things.

questions.q: The Sun is biggest and hottest in our sky because it is...
options: made of fire like a candle
questions.explain: The Sun is the star closest to Earth.

questions.q: Solar panels on a roof use sunlight to make...
questions.explain: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity.

questions.q: Why does the Sun seem to change position from morning to evening?
options: Earth's spinning changes what we see
questions.explain: Earth rotates, so the Sun appears in different places in our sky.

questions.q: A sundial tells time by using...
questions.explain: A sundial uses the moving shadow cast by sunlight to show the time.

questions.q: Which is TRUE about the Sun?
options: It reflects light from the Moon
It is a star that gives off its own light
It is cold at the center
questions.explain: The Sun makes its own light. The Moon only reflects sunlight.

questions.q: Morning shadows point west. Afternoon shadows point...
questions.explain: Shadows always point away from the Sun, so afternoon shadows point east.

questions.q: What keeps Earth moving around the Sun instead of flying away?
questions.explain: The Sun's gravity holds Earth in its orbit.

rounds.title: Year Quest: Earth, Sun & Moon - Quest 2
rounds.desc: The Sun is a star that gives us light and heat. Study its path and your changing shadow.

title: Year Quest: Earth, Sun & Moon - Quest 3
subject: Kids Science
description: The Moon reflects sunlight and changes phases. Plus: why Earth's tilt gives us seasons.

questions.q: Why does the Moon shine at night?
options: It reflects light from the Sun
questions.explain: The Moon does not make light. It reflects sunlight, like a mirror.

questions.q: Does the Moon make its own light?
options: Yes, on full moon nights only
questions.explain: The Moon shines because sunlight bounces off its surface.

questions.q: What does the Moon move around?
questions.explain: The Moon orbits Earth.

questions.q: About how long does the Moon take to orbit Earth once?
questions.explain: The Moon takes about a month to travel around Earth.

questions.q: When the whole lit face of the Moon points at Earth, we see a...
questions.explain: A full moon appears when we see the whole sunlit side.

questions.q: When the Moon's lit side faces away from Earth, we see a...
questions.explain: At new moon, the lit side faces away, so the Moon looks dark in our sky.

questions.q: A thin sliver of lit Moon is called a...
questions.explain: A crescent moon shows just a thin curved sliver of light.

questions.q: Why does the Moon seem to change shape in the sky?
options: We see different amounts of its sunlit half as it orbits Earth
It spins like a ball each night
questions.explain: The Moon's phases come from seeing different parts of its sunlit half.

questions.q: What are the dark round marks and dips on the Moon's surface called?
questions.explain: Craters are dips made long ago when space rocks hit the Moon.

questions.q: How does the Moon compare to Earth in size?
options: They are exactly the same size
The Moon is smaller than Earth
The Moon is bigger than the Sun
The Moon is bigger than Earth
questions.explain: The Moon is about one fourth as wide as Earth.

questions.q: Has anyone ever walked on the Moon?
options: Yes, astronauts landed and walked there
questions.explain: Astronauts first landed on the Moon in 1969.

questions.q: Why do seasons change on Earth?
options: Earth is tilted as it orbits the Sun, so sunlight hits parts of Earth differently during the year
The Moon blocks heat in winter
The Sun gets hotter and colder
Earth moves much closer to the Sun in summer
questions.explain: Seasons change because Earth's tilt points parts of the planet toward or away from the Sun during its orbit.

questions.q: In United States summer, our part of Earth is...
questions.explain: In summer, the Northern Hemisphere tilts toward the Sun and gets stronger sunlight.

questions.q: In United States winter, our part of Earth is...
questions.explain: In winter, the Northern Hemisphere tilts away from the Sun and gets weaker sunlight.

questions.q: Can you sometimes see the Moon during the day?
options: Yes, the Moon can be in the daytime sky
No, the Moon only exists at night
No, the Sun hides it completely
questions.explain: The Moon orbits Earth, so it is often in the sky during the day too.

questions.q: The Moon's gravity helps cause...
questions.explain: The pull of the Moon's gravity helps cause tides in the oceans.

questions.q: What is the changing pattern of the Moon's lit shapes called?
questions.explain: The repeating pattern of new, crescent, half, and full is called the Moon's phases.

questions.q: After a full moon, the lit part we see will...
options: jump to new moon in one night
questions.explain: After full moon, the lit part shrinks night by night until new moon.

questions.q: Which object is a natural satellite (a moon) of Earth?
questions.explain: Earth's one natural satellite is the Moon.

questions.q: Astronauts found the Moon's surface to be...
options: rocky and dusty, with no air to breathe
questions.explain: The Moon is rocky and dusty and has almost no air, so astronauts wore space suits.

The Moon covers the Sun all night
The Sun goes to sleep at night
questions.explain: Earth rotates once each day. The side facing the Sun has daytime.

questions.q: When your side of Earth faces the Sun, it is... (Review)
questions.explain: The side of Earth facing the Sun is lit up: it is daytime there.

questions.q: When your side of Earth faces away from the Sun, it is... (Review)
questions.explain: The side of Earth facing away from the Sun is dark: it is nighttime there.

questions.q: How long does Earth take to spin around once? (Review)
questions.explain: Earth makes one full rotation in about 24 hours, giving us day and night.

questions.q: How long does Earth take to travel all the way around the Sun? (Review)
questions.explain: Earth orbits the Sun once each year.

questions.q: The Sun rises in the... (Review)
questions.explain: The Sun appears to rise in the east and set in the west because Earth spins.

questions.q: The Sun sets in the... (Review)
questions.explain: The Sun appears to set in the west.

questions.q: When is the Sun highest in the sky? (Review)
options: Around the middle of the day (noon)
questions.explain: The Sun reaches its highest point around noon.

questions.q: Your shadow is longest... (Review)
options: in the early morning and late afternoon
questions.explain: When the Sun is low, shadows are long. At noon, shadows are short.

questions.q: At noon on a sunny day, your shadow is... (Review)
options: gone to the other side of Earth
questions.explain: When the Sun is high overhead, shadows are short.

questions.q: Why does the Moon shine at night? (Review)
options: It reflects light from the Sun
questions.explain: The Moon does not make light. It reflects sunlight, like a mirror.

questions.q: Does the Moon make its own light? (Review)
options: Yes, on full moon nights only
questions.explain: The Moon shines because sunlight bounces off its surface.

questions.q: What does the Moon move around? (Review)
questions.explain: The Moon orbits Earth.

questions.q: About how long does the Moon take to orbit Earth once? (Review)
questions.explain: The Moon takes about a month to travel around Earth.

questions.q: When the whole lit face of the Moon points at Earth, we see a... (Review)
questions.explain: A full moon appears when we see the whole sunlit side.

questions.q: It is midnight where you live. Why can't you see the Sun?
options: Clouds always cover it at night
Your side of Earth is facing away from the Sun
questions.explain: At midnight your side of Earth faces away from the Sun, so it is night.

questions.q: Why can we see stars better at night?
options: Stars hide behind the Sun all day
The sky is dark because our side of Earth faces away from the Sun
Stars only come out at night
The Moon turns the stars on
questions.explain: Stars shine all the time, but sunlight makes the daytime sky too bright to see them.

questions.q: Earth is which planet from the Sun?
questions.explain: Counting from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, then Earth third.

questions.q: A class uses a lamp and a ball to model the Moon shining. What does the lamp stand for, and why does the ball shine?
options: The lamp is Earth; the ball is a mirror moon
The lamp is a star; the ball glows by itself
The lamp is the Moon; the ball makes its own light
The lamp is the Sun; the ball reflects its light like the Moon reflects sunlight
questions.explain: The Moon reflects sunlight, just like the ball reflects the lamp's light.

questions.q: Which list puts these in order from biggest to smallest?
questions.explain: The Sun is biggest, then Earth, then the Moon.

rounds.title: Year Quest: Earth, Sun & Moon - Quest 4
rounds.desc: Boss quest: day, night, Sun, Moon, and seasons - the ultimate space review.

title: Year Quest: Matter: Solids, Liquids & Gases - Quest 1
subject: Kids Science
description: Solids keep their shape. Sort and describe the solids all around you.

questions.q: Ava is sorting things by state of matter. Which one is a solid?
questions.explain: A solid keeps its own shape and does not flow.

questions.q: Liam looks at four things. Which one is a solid?
questions.explain: A solid keeps its own shape and does not flow.

questions.q: Mia needs an example of a solid for a poster. Which should Mia pick?
questions.explain: A solid keeps its own shape and does not flow.

questions.q: Noah wonders: which of these is a solid?
questions.explain: A solid keeps its own shape and does not flow.

questions.q: Zoe is playing a guessing game. Which one is a solid?
questions.explain: A solid keeps its own shape and does not flow.

questions.q: Eli is sorting things by state of matter. Which one is a solid?
options: the air inside a beach ball
questions.explain: A solid keeps its own shape and does not flow.

questions.q: Ruby looks at four things. Which one is a solid?
options: the gas that fills a soap bubble
questions.explain: A solid keeps its own shape and does not flow.

questions.q: Owen needs an example of a solid for a poster. Which should Owen pick?
questions.explain: A solid keeps its own shape and does not flow.

questions.q: Lily wonders: which of these is a solid?
questions.explain: A solid keeps its own shape and does not flow.

questions.q: Max is playing a guessing game. Which one is a solid?
questions.explain: A solid keeps its own shape and does not flow.

questions.q: What is true of all solids?
questions.explain: Solids keep their own shape. A block stays a block in any container.

questions.q: A pillow is soft and squishy. Is a pillow a solid?
options: No. All solids are hard as rocks
Yes. It keeps its shape and does not flow
questions.explain: Soft things can be solids too. A pillow is a solid because it holds its shape.

questions.q: Which word describes how the surface of sandpaper feels?
questions.explain: We describe matter with words like rough, smooth, hard, and soft.

questions.q: Which solid can melt when it gets warm?
questions.explain: Ice is frozen water, a solid that melts into liquid water when warmed.

questions.q: Why doesn't a book change shape when you put it in a box?
options: It is a solid, and solids keep their shape
The box holds it still forever
questions.explain: Solids keep their own shape no matter what container they are in.

questions.q: Which of these is a describing word (property) for matter?
questions.explain: Properties of matter include hard, soft, rough, smooth, heavy, and light.

questions.q: Two solids can be sorted by...
options: their size, shape, color, or texture
questions.explain: We can sort matter by its properties, like size, shape, color, and texture.

questions.q: Which solid is made by freezing water?
questions.explain: Ice is water frozen into a solid.

questions.q: A marble rolls but keeps its round shape. A marble is a...
questions.explain: A marble is a solid. It keeps its shape even when it moves.

questions.q: Which group has ONLY solids?
questions.explain: Rocks, sticks, and coins are all solids.

rounds.title: Year Quest: Matter: Solids, Liquids & Gases - Quest 1
rounds.desc: Solids keep their shape. Sort and describe the solids all around you.

title: Year Quest: Matter: Solids, Liquids & Gases - Quest 2
subject: Kids Science
description: Liquids flow and take the shape of their container. Pour into the world of liquids.

questions.q: Mia is sorting things by state of matter. Which one is a liquid?
questions.explain: A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.

questions.q: Noah looks at four things. Which one is a liquid?
questions.explain: A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.

questions.q: Zoe needs an example of a liquid for a poster. Which should Zoe pick?
questions.explain: A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.

questions.q: Eli wonders: which of these is a liquid?
questions.explain: A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.

questions.q: Ruby is playing a guessing game. Which one is a liquid?
questions.explain: A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.

questions.q: Owen is sorting things by state of matter. Which one is a liquid?
options: the air inside a beach ball
questions.explain: A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.

questions.q: Lily looks at four things. Which one is a liquid?
options: the gas that fills a soap bubble
questions.explain: A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.

questions.q: Max needs an example of a liquid for a poster. Which should Max pick?
questions.explain: A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.

questions.q: What happens when you pour water from a tall glass into a wide bowl?
options: The water takes the shape of the bowl
The water turns into a solid
The water keeps the tall glass shape
questions.explain: Liquids flow and take the shape of their container.

questions.q: Why does juice fill the bottom of a cup instead of standing in a tall pile?
options: Cups push juice down with hands
questions.explain: Liquids cannot hold a shape, so they flow and spread out.

questions.q: Honey pours very slowly, but it still pours. Honey is a...
questions.explain: Honey is a thick liquid. Thick liquids flow slowly.

questions.q: Which of these can you pour?
questions.explain: Liquids can be poured. Milk is a liquid.

questions.q: What do we call the flat top surface of water in a glass?
options: It stays level (flat) because liquid spreads out
It piles up in a point
questions.explain: The surface of a liquid in a container stays flat and level.

questions.q: If you spill water on the table, it spreads into a puddle. That is because water is a...
questions.explain: Liquids flow and spread out when they are not in a container.

questions.q: Which group has ONLY liquids?
questions.explain: Milk, juice, and oil are all liquids.

questions.q: Measuring cups are used to measure...
questions.explain: We measure liquids with measuring cups and spoons.

questions.q: What happens to a liquid's shape when its container changes?
options: Its shape changes to match the new container
questions.explain: A liquid takes the shape of whatever container holds it.

questions.q: Rain is which state of matter?
questions.explain: Rain is liquid water falling from clouds.

questions.q: Which of these liquids flows the SLOWEST when poured?
questions.explain: Honey is a very thick liquid, so it flows much more slowly than water or milk.

questions.q: Which of these is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.explain: Vegetable oil is a liquid. Ice is a solid until it melts.

rounds.title: Year Quest: Matter: Solids, Liquids & Gases - Quest 2
rounds.desc: Liquids flow and take the shape of their container. Pour into the world of liquids.

title: Year Quest: Matter: Solids, Liquids & Gases - Quest 3
subject: Kids Science
description: Gases spread out to fill any space. Meet the invisible gases, including air itself.

questions.q: Zoe is sorting things by state of matter. Which one is a gas?
questions.explain: A gas spreads out to fill the space it is in.

questions.q: Eli looks at four things. Which one is a gas?
questions.explain: A gas spreads out to fill the space it is in.

questions.q: Ruby needs an example of a gas for a poster. Which should Ruby pick?
questions.explain: A gas spreads out to fill the space it is in.

questions.q: Owen wonders: which of these is a gas?
options: the air inside a beach ball
questions.explain: A gas spreads out to fill the space it is in.

questions.q: Lily is playing a guessing game. Which one is a gas?
questions.explain: A gas spreads out to fill the space it is in.

questions.q: Max is sorting things by state of matter. Which one is a gas?
options: the gas that fills a soap bubble
questions.explain: A gas spreads out to fill the space it is in.

questions.q: What is true of most gases?
options: They can be picked up like a rock
They spread out to fill all the space they can
They always sink into a pile
questions.explain: Gases spread out and fill the whole space available to them.

questions.q: Why does a balloon get bigger when you blow into it?
options: The balloon grows like a plant
The air you add fills and stretches the balloon
questions.explain: Air is a gas. Added air spreads out and pushes the balloon bigger.

questions.q: Can you see the air in a room?
options: No, air is invisible, but you can feel it when it moves as wind
questions.explain: Air is a gas we cannot see, but moving air (wind) can be felt.

questions.q: A beach ball feels firm when it is full. What is inside pushing out?
questions.explain: A beach ball is filled with air, a gas.

questions.q: What is wind?
questions.explain: Wind is air in motion.

questions.q: Steam rising from hot soup is...
questions.explain: Steam is water that has changed into a gas, called water vapor.

questions.q: Which of these shows that air takes up space?
options: A rock sinking in a pond
A bubble of air trapped under an upside-down cup in water
questions.explain: Air takes up space, so it can be trapped as a bubble in water.

questions.q: If you squeeze a sealed, air-filled bag, it pushes back. Why?
options: The gas inside is pressed into a smaller space and pushes back
questions.explain: Gases can be squeezed into smaller spaces, and they push back.

questions.q: Which group has ONLY gases?
options: Helium, juice, oxygen in a tank
questions.explain: Air, helium, and water vapor are gases. (Oxygen in a tank is a gas too, but juice is a liquid.)

questions.q: Bubbles in soda pop are made of...
questions.explain: The fizz in soda is a gas coming out of the liquid.

questions.q: Why do bike tires need to be pumped up?
options: Air makes the tire heavier than a car
Air inside pushes out to make the tire firm
questions.explain: Pumped-up tires are firm because the air inside pushes outward.

questions.q: Which state of matter is the oxygen we breathe?
questions.explain: Oxygen is a gas in the air that living things need.

questions.q: A diver's tank holds air squeezed into a small space. This shows gases can be...
questions.explain: Gases can be compressed into a smaller space, like air in a diving tank.

questions.q: Smoke from a campfire spreads out through the air. Smoke behaves most like...
options: a liquid taking a cup's shape
questions.explain: Smoke spreads out and mixes with air, much like a gas spreading to fill space.

rounds.title: Year Quest: Matter: Solids, Liquids & Gases - Quest 3
rounds.desc: Gases spread out to fill any space. Meet the invisible gases, including air itself.

title: Year Quest: Matter: Solids, Liquids & Gases - Quest 4
subject: Kids Science
description: Boss quest: melting, freezing, evaporating - master how matter changes state.

questions.q: An ice cube sits in a warm room and turns into a puddle of water. This change is called...
questions.explain: Melting is when a solid changes into a liquid, usually by warming up.

questions.q: Water is put in a freezer and turns into ice. This change is called...
questions.explain: Freezing is when a liquid changes into a solid by getting cold.

questions.q: What happens to chocolate held in a warm hand?
options: It melts from a solid into a gooey liquid
It turns into a gas at once
questions.explain: Warmth melts chocolate, changing it from a solid toward a liquid.

questions.q: Butter in a hot pan changes from a solid pat to a liquid. What caused the change?
questions.explain: Heating a solid like butter can melt it into a liquid.

questions.q: A puddle slowly shrinks on a hot day as water becomes vapor. This is...
questions.explain: Evaporation is liquid water changing into water vapor, a gas.

questions.q: Droplets form on the outside of a cold juice box. This is...
options: condensation: water vapor in the air turning into liquid
questions.explain: Condensation happens when water vapor cools and changes back into liquid drops.

questions.q: To turn liquid water into ice, you should...
questions.explain: Water freezes into ice when it gets cold enough (0 degrees Celsius).

questions.q: To turn ice back into liquid water, you should...
questions.explain: Warming ice melts it back into liquid water.

questions.q: Is melting a change that can be undone?
options: No. Changes can never be undone
Yes. Melted water can be frozen back into ice
questions.explain: Melting and freezing are reversible: water can change back and forth.

questions.q: Lava flowing from a volcano is rock that is...
options: so hot it has melted into a liquid
questions.explain: Rock deep underground can get hot enough to melt into liquid lava.

questions.q: Which change needs HEAT added?
questions.explain: Melting needs heat. Freezing and dew happen when things get colder.

questions.q: Which change happens when something gets COLDER?
questions.explain: Condensation happens when water vapor cools and becomes liquid.

questions.q: A wet towel dries faster on a warm, sunny day than on a cold day. Why?
questions.explain: Heat gives water energy to evaporate faster.

questions.q: Steam from a kettle hits a cold window and turns into drops. The drops formed by...
questions.explain: Water vapor condenses into liquid drops on a cold surface.

questions.q: Which is the right order for making an ice pop?
options: Eat the juice, then freeze the stick, then pour it
Pour the mold, eat the freezer, then freeze the juice
Pour juice (liquid) into a mold, freeze it into a solid, then eat it before it melts
Freeze juice into a solid, pour the solid, then melt it into the mold
questions.explain: Juice is a liquid. Freezing turns it into a solid ice pop.

questions.q: Snow is which state of matter, and what can it do in spring?
options: A solid that can melt into liquid water
A liquid that can evaporate only
A solid that can never change
questions.explain: Snow is solid water. In warmer spring weather, it melts.

questions.q: What do we call how hot or cold something is?
questions.explain: Temperature tells how hot or cold matter is, and temperature changes can change its state.

questions.q: A scientist says matter is...
options: anything that takes up space and has mass (weight)
questions.explain: Matter is anything that takes up space and has mass. Solids, liquids, and gases are its states.

questions.q: Which list names the three states of matter in this unit?
questions.explain: The three states of matter are solid, liquid, and gas.

questions.q: Hot soup, the bowl, and the steam: which is which?
options: Soup is solid, the bowl is gas, the steam is liquid
Soup is gas, the bowl is liquid, the steam is solid
Soup is liquid, the bowl is solid, the steam is gas
questions.explain: Soup is a liquid, a bowl is a solid, and steam is a gas (water vapor).

rounds.title: Year Quest: Matter: Solids, Liquids & Gases - Quest 4
rounds.desc: Boss quest: melting, freezing, evaporating - master how matter changes state.

questions.q: What is a force?
questions.explain: In science, a force is a push or a pull on something.

questions.q: When you push a toy car, what can the push do?
options: Turn it into a real car
Start it moving, speed it up, slow it down, or change its direction
questions.explain: Forces can start, stop, speed up, slow down, or turn moving things.

questions.q: A magnet pulls a paper clip without touching it. The magnet uses a...
questions.explain: Magnets can pull some metal objects without touching them.

questions.q: Gravity is a force that...
questions.explain: Gravity pulls objects toward Earth, which is why things fall down.

title: Year Quest: Pushes, Pulls & Simple Machines - Quest 2
subject: Kids Science
description: Friction, gravity, and speed: learn what starts, stops, and slows moving things.

questions.q: Two balls are pushed with the same force. One rolls on smooth ice and one on thick carpet. Which rolls farther?
questions.explain: Friction slows things down. Thick carpet has more friction than smooth ice.

questions.q: What is friction?
options: A force that slows down things rubbing against each other
A force that speeds everything up
questions.explain: Friction acts between touching surfaces and slows motion.

questions.q: A soccer ball rolls across the grass and slowly stops. Why?
options: The grass pushed it backward with hands
Friction between the ball and grass slows it down
questions.explain: Friction slows the rolling ball until it stops.

questions.q: If you push a toy car harder, what usually happens?
questions.explain: A stronger push is a bigger force, so the car moves faster and farther.

questions.q: A marble rolls off a table. Which force pulls it down to the floor?
questions.explain: Gravity pulls the marble down toward Earth.

questions.q: Which surface gives the LEAST friction for a sled?
questions.explain: Smooth surfaces like ice have very little friction.

questions.q: Why do shoes have rough, bumpy soles?
options: Friction helps the shoes grip the ground so you do not slip
questions.explain: Rough soles increase friction and grip, which keeps you from slipping.

questions.q: A ball is rolling toward you and you kick it back the other way. Your kick changed the ball's...
questions.explain: A force can change the direction of a moving object.

questions.q: Which needs the BIGGEST force to move?
options: A heavy box full of books
questions.explain: Heavier objects need bigger forces to start them moving.

questions.q: A wagon rolls downhill and goes faster and faster. What is pulling it down?
questions.explain: Gravity pulls the wagon down the hill, speeding it up.

questions.q: Two ramps: one smooth wood, one covered in rough sandpaper. A toy car rolls farther on the...
questions.explain: Less friction on the smooth ramp lets the car roll farther.

questions.q: What happens when the forces on a still object are removed and nothing pushes or pulls it?
questions.explain: Objects stay still unless a force pushes or pulls them.

questions.q: A goalie catches a fast soccer ball. The goalie's hands apply a force that...
questions.explain: A catching force stops a moving ball.

questions.q: Which is an example of changing an object's speed?
options: Parking a bike in a picture
questions.explain: Pedaling harder adds force and increases the bike's speed.

questions.q: Oil is put on a squeaky door hinge to...
options: reduce friction so the door swings easily
questions.explain: Oil makes surfaces slippery, reducing friction.

questions.q: A parachute slows a falling skydiver mainly by...
options: catching lots of air, which pushes up against the fall
questions.explain: The wide parachute pushes against the air, slowing the fall.

questions.q: Why does a rolling ball on a smooth floor eventually stop, even with no wall?
options: Friction (and air) slowly take away its motion
Balls always stop after ten seconds
questions.explain: Friction between the ball and floor, plus air resistance, slows it to a stop.

questions.q: Which force helps a car stop when the driver uses the brakes?
options: Friction in the brakes and tires
questions.explain: Brakes use friction to slow the wheels and stop the car.

questions.q: A paper airplane thrown gently lands close by. Thrown hard, it lands far away. What changed?
options: The size of the throwing force
questions.explain: A bigger throwing force sends the plane farther.

questions.q: What does the word motion mean?
options: Moving from one place to another (a change in position)
questions.explain: Motion is a change in position. Forces cause motion to start, stop, or change.

rounds.title: Year Quest: Pushes, Pulls & Simple Machines - Quest 2

title: Year Quest: Pushes, Pulls & Simple Machines - Quest 3
subject: Kids Science
description: Levers, ramps, pulleys, wheels, screws, and wedges: meet the six simple machines.

questions.q: Which simple machine is a seesaw an example of?
questions.explain: A seesaw is an example of a lever.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a lever?
options: a loading ramp into a truck
a crowbar lifting a heavy rock
questions.explain: A a crowbar lifting a heavy rock is a lever.

questions.q: Which simple machine is a wheelchair ramp an example of?
questions.explain: A wheelchair ramp is an example of an inclined plane (ramp).

questions.q: Which of these is an example of an inclined plane (ramp)?
options: a loading ramp into a truck
questions.explain: A a loading ramp into a truck is an inclined plane (ramp).

questions.q: Which simple machine is a flagpole rope an example of?
questions.explain: A flagpole rope is an example of a pulley.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a pulley?
options: the rope and wheel that raise window blinds
questions.explain: A the rope and wheel that raise window blinds is a pulley.

questions.q: Which simple machine is a bicycle wheel an example of?
questions.explain: A bicycle wheel is an example of a wheel and axle.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a wheel and axle?
options: a loading ramp into a truck
questions.explain: A a doorknob is a wheel and axle.

questions.q: Which simple machine is a jar lid an example of?
questions.explain: A jar lid is an example of a screw.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a screw?
options: a wood screw holding boards together
questions.explain: A a wood screw holding boards together is a screw.

questions.q: Which simple machine is an axe splitting wood an example of?
questions.explain: An axe splitting wood is an example of a wedge.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a wedge?
options: a crowbar lifting a heavy rock
questions.explain: A a doorstop is a wedge.

questions.q: What is a simple machine?
options: A tool with few or no moving parts that makes work easier
questions.explain: Simple machines like levers and ramps help us move or lift things with less force.

questions.q: Why does a ramp make loading a heavy box into a truck easier?
options: The box becomes lighter in weight forever
You push the box up a gentle slope instead of lifting it straight up
The ramp lifts the box by itself
questions.explain: A ramp spreads the lifting over a longer, gentler path, so it takes less force.

questions.q: A seesaw is a lever. Where is its turning point (fulcrum)?
options: In the middle, where the seesaw rests on its support
At the very end of the board
questions.explain: A lever turns on a point called the fulcrum.

questions.q: How does a pulley help raise a flag?
options: The flag floats up by itself
Wind does all the work always
Pulling down on the rope lifts the flag up
questions.explain: A pulley changes the direction of a force, so pulling down raises the flag.

questions.q: Wheels help heavy things move by...
questions.explain: Wheels roll, and rolling has much less friction than dragging.

questions.q: A screw is most like which simple machine wrapped around a post?
questions.explain: A screw's threads are like a ramp wrapped around a cylinder.

questions.q: A wedge works by...
options: pushing things apart, like an axe splitting wood
questions.explain: A wedge is pushed into something to split or lift it apart.

questions.q: Which simple machine would best help you lift a piano onto a porch?
options: A flagpole pulley tied to the roof only
An inclined plane (ramp) to roll or slide it up
questions.explain: A ramp lets you move a heavy piano up with less force than lifting.

questions.explain: For the job of raise a flag to the top of a pole, a pulley works best.

questions.q: Which simple machine is best for this job: move a heavy box up into a truck?
questions.explain: For the job of move a heavy box up into a truck, an inclined plane (ramp) works best.

questions.q: Which simple machine is best for this job: lift one end of a heavy rock to slip a board under it?
questions.explain: For the job of lift one end of a heavy rock to slip a board under it, a lever works best.

questions.q: Which simple machine is best for this job: move a wagon full of bricks across a yard?
questions.explain: For the job of move a wagon full of bricks across a yard, wheels and axles works best.

questions.q: Which simple machine is best for this job: split a log into firewood?
questions.explain: For the job of split a log into firewood, a wedge works best.

questions.q: Which simple machine is best for this job: hold two boards tightly together?
questions.explain: For the job of hold two boards tightly together, a screw works best.

questions.q: Which simple machine is best for this job: lift a bucket of water from a well?
questions.explain: For the job of lift a bucket of water from a well, a pulley works best.

questions.q: Which simple machine is best for this job: help a person in a wheelchair reach a higher doorway?
questions.explain: For the job of help a person in a wheelchair reach a higher doorway, an inclined plane (ramp) works best.

questions.q: A playground seesaw, a flagpole, and a wheelchair ramp are all...
options: simple machines that make work easier
questions.explain: Levers, pulleys, and ramps are simple machines.

questions.q: Which action is a PULL?
questions.explain: Reeling in a kite string pulls the kite toward you.

questions.q: Which action is a PUSH?
questions.explain: Pressing a key pushes it down and away.

questions.q: A heavy door is hard to open when you push near its hinges, but easy when you push near the handle. The door works like a...
questions.explain: A door swings on its hinges like a lever, and pushing far from the hinge gives more turning force.

questions.q: Why do moving trucks have ramps instead of just lifting boxes in?
options: Lifting is against the rules of science
Ramps make the work easier by using less force over a longer path
questions.explain: An inclined plane (ramp) reduces the force needed to raise heavy things.

questions.q: What force must you overcome to slide a heavy box across the floor?
options: Friction between the box and the floor
questions.explain: Friction fights against the sliding, so you must push hard to overcome it.

questions.q: A flag rises as Sam pulls the rope down. The flagpole uses a...
questions.explain: A pulley at the top of the flagpole lets a downward pull raise the flag.

questions.q: Which is the best tool to split a piece of wood?
questions.explain: An axe is a wedge that splits wood apart.

questions.q: Two kids of different weights sit on a seesaw. The heavier kid sits closer to the middle. Why?
options: It makes the heavier kid lighter
Moving closer to the fulcrum balances the lever
questions.explain: On a lever, weight closer to the fulcrum balances weight farther away.

questions.q: A jar lid twists off. The threads on the jar work like a...
questions.explain: Jar lid threads act like a screw, turning a twist into a strong grip or release.

questions.q: Which simple machine is inside a rolling suitcase handle system that lets it glide?
questions.explain: Suitcase wheels on axles let heavy bags roll with little friction.

questions.q: What do all simple machines have in common?
options: They help people do work with less force or in an easier direction
questions.explain: Simple machines trade force or direction to make work easier.

questions.q: What does recycle mean?
options: To bury trash in the yard
To throw everything in a river
To use something once and waste it
To turn used materials into new things
questions.explain: Recycling collects materials like paper, cans, and glass and makes them into new products.

questions.q: What does reuse mean?
options: To buy new things every day
To use something again instead of throwing it away
questions.explain: Reusing means using an item again, like refilling a water bottle.

questions.q: What does reduce mean in the three Rs?
options: To use less and make less trash in the first place
To buy the biggest package always

questions.q: Which list names the three Rs for helping Earth?
questions.explain: The three Rs are reduce, reuse, and recycle.

questions.q: Why do we recycle aluminum cans?

questions.explain: Recycling cans saves energy and natural resources.

questions.q: A refillable water bottle helps Earth because...
options: it makes water cleaner by magic
it reduces plastic trash by being used again and again
plastic bottles disappear on their own
questions.explain: Reusing a bottle keeps many single-use plastic bottles out of the trash.

questions.q: Compost is...
options: rotted food scraps and yard waste that enrich garden soil
questions.explain: Compost turns food scraps into rich material that helps gardens grow.

questions.q: Which of these should NEVER go in a recycling bin?
options: A greasy pizza box soaked with cheese (it goes in trash or compost where allowed)
questions.explain: Food-soiled paper cannot be recycled well. Clean paper, cans, and glass can.

title: Year Quest: Caring for Our Planet - Quest 2
subject: Kids Science
description: Save water and energy with everyday habits at home and school.

questions.q: You are about to brush your teeth. Which choice saves resources?
options: Leave the water running the whole time
Turn off the water while you brush
Leave all the lights on all day
Let the faucet drip for weeks
questions.explain: Small habits save water and energy every day.

questions.q: You are about to leave a room. Which choice saves resources?
options: Let the faucet drip for weeks
Turn on every lamp at noon
questions.explain: Small habits save water and energy every day.

questions.q: You are about to see a dripping faucet. Which choice saves resources?
options: Tell an adult so it can be fixed
Turn on every lamp at noon
Leave the TV on all night
Throw the can in the bushes
questions.explain: Small habits save water and energy every day.

questions.q: You are about to take a shower. Which choice saves resources?
options: Leave the water running the whole time
Keep it short instead of very long
Leave the TV on all night
Water at the hottest time so it dries up fast
questions.explain: Small habits save water and energy every day.

questions.q: You are about to play outside on a sunny day. Which choice saves resources?
options: Leave all the lights on all day
Let the faucet drip for weeks
Leave the water running the whole time
Use daylight instead of turning on lamps
questions.explain: Small habits save water and energy every day.

questions.q: You are about to finish a drink from a can. Which choice saves resources?
options: Rinse the can and recycle it
Turn on every lamp at noon
Let the faucet drip for weeks
questions.explain: Small habits save water and energy every day.

questions.q: You are about to go to bed. Which choice saves resources?
options: Throw the can in the bushes
Turn off the TV and lights
Leave the TV on all night
Turn on every lamp at noon
questions.explain: Small habits save water and energy every day.

questions.q: You are about to water the garden. Which choice saves resources?
options: Leave the water running the whole time
Water at the hottest time so it dries up fast
Leave the TV on all night
Water in the cooler morning so less evaporates
questions.explain: Small habits save water and energy every day.

questions.q: Why should we save water?
options: Water will run out tomorrow for sure
Water is not needed by farms
Clean water is precious, and people, plants, and animals all need it
Saving water is only for fun
questions.explain: Fresh water is limited in many places, and all living things need it.

questions.q: Which action saves the MOST water at home?
options: Fixing a leaky faucet that drips all day
Filling the tub to the top for a small bath
questions.explain: A dripping faucet can waste many gallons of water, so fixing leaks saves a lot.

questions.q: Turning off lights when you leave a room saves...
questions.explain: Lights use electricity. Turning them off saves energy.

questions.q: Which is a good way to save energy in winter?
options: Wear a swimsuit and turn heat to maximum
Open windows with the heat on high
Close doors and wear a sweater indoors instead of blasting the heat
questions.explain: Keeping warm air in and dressing warmly saves heating energy.

questions.q: Walking or biking on a short trip instead of riding in a car helps by...
options: using no fuel and keeping the air cleaner
questions.explain: Walking and biking use no fuel, so they keep air cleaner.

questions.q: Why is it good to turn off the tap while soaping your hands?
options: It saves water that would run down the drain unused
Water disappears forever if it runs
Soap works only in dry hands
questions.explain: Water running while you soap is wasted. Turning it off saves it.

questions.q: A class plants a tree at school. How does the tree help the planet?
options: It cleans the air, gives shade, and is a home for animals
It uses up all the sunlight
questions.explain: Trees clean the air, cool the ground with shade, and shelter wildlife.

questions.q: Which choice saves paper?
options: Using a new sheet for every word
Printing ten copies you do not need
Writing on both sides of a sheet
questions.explain: Using both sides of paper halves paper waste.

questions.q: What can happen to sea animals when plastic trash reaches the ocean?
options: They use it to build houses
They can eat it or get tangled in it and be harmed
questions.explain: Ocean plastic harms sea animals, so keeping trash out of waterways matters.

questions.q: Why do people put solar panels on roofs?
options: To block the sun from Earth
To make electricity from sunlight without burning fuel
To catch rain for drinking only
questions.explain: Solar panels turn sunlight into clean electricity.

questions.q: Which is the best reason to bring a reusable lunch box?
options: It creates less trash than throwaway bags every day
It makes lunch taste like candy
questions.explain: Reusable containers cut down daily trash.

questions.q: If everyone in a class turned off one light for an hour, the class would...
options: make the room colder like winter
questions.explain: Small savings add up when many people help.

title: Year Quest: Caring for Our Planet - Quest 3
subject: Kids Science
description: Clean air, clean water, and safe habitats: learn how to protect nature and animals.

questions.q: Why does litter on the ground hurt animals?
options: Animals can eat it or get tangled in it
questions.explain: Litter is dangerous. Animals can swallow it or get stuck in it.

questions.q: You see a plastic bag blowing toward a stream. What is the best thing to do?
options: Pick it up and put it in the trash
Let it go into the water
questions.explain: Keeping plastic out of streams protects water animals.

questions.q: Why should we plant flowers for bees and butterflies?
options: They need flower nectar for food, and they help pollinate plants
questions.explain: Bees and butterflies feed on flowers and carry pollen that helps plants make seeds.

questions.q: A park sign says stay on the path and do not pick the wildflowers. Why?
options: Wildflowers feed insects and make seeds for new flowers
The flowers are dangerous to look at
questions.explain: Leaving wildflowers lets them feed insects and spread seeds.

questions.q: What happens when oil or soap pollution gets into a river?
options: It can harm fish and other water animals
Fish love soap in their water
questions.explain: Pollution in water harms the animals and plants that live there.

questions.q: How do trees help clean the air?
options: They take in a gas (carbon dioxide) and give off oxygen
They blow air away with leaves only
They hide dirty air behind them
They sweep dust with branches like brooms
questions.explain: Trees absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen, cleaning the air.

questions.q: Why is it important to keep some wild places, like forests and wetlands, unbuilt?
options: They are homes for many plants and animals
questions.explain: Wild habitats shelter wildlife and keep nature in balance.

questions.q: A bird built a nest in a bush near your home. What is the kind thing to do?
options: Watch from far away and leave the nest alone
Move the nest to your room
questions.explain: Watching from a distance keeps baby birds safe with their parents.

questions.q: Why should you never feed wild animals human snacks?
options: Animals do not like snacks at all
It makes them grow too fast to fly
Snacks turn into litter by magic
Human food can make them sick and teach them to depend on people
questions.explain: Wild animals need their natural foods. Human snacks can harm them.

questions.q: Picking up trash at a beach helps sea turtles because...
options: bags are turtle food otherwise, which is fine
turtles will not mistake plastic bags for food
turtles like clean sand for dancing
questions.explain: Sea turtles can mistake plastic bags for jellyfish, their food, and get sick.

questions.q: What is one way kids can help birds in winter?
options: Put out a bird feeder with seeds
Chase birds to keep them warm
questions.explain: Bird feeders give birds extra food when winter food is scarce.

questions.q: Why do wetlands (marshes) matter?
options: They clean water and are homes for frogs, birds, and fish
They block all water from flowing
questions.explain: Wetlands filter water and shelter many living things.

questions.q: Smoke from factories and cars can make the air dirty. Dirty air is called...
questions.explain: Air pollution is harmful material in the air from smoke and exhaust.

questions.q: What is a habitat loss problem for animals?
options: When forests are cut down, animals lose their homes
When it rains in a forest
questions.explain: Clearing forests destroys the homes animals depend on.

questions.q: Why do gardeners avoid sprays that kill all insects?
options: Bees do not matter to gardens
Sprays make plants grow too fast
Helpful insects like bees and ladybugs would be harmed too
questions.explain: Some insects help gardens by pollinating and eating pests.

questions.q: A class recycles paper all year. How does that help forests?
options: It turns old paper into soil instantly
Recycled paper means fewer trees need to be cut for new paper
questions.explain: Recycling paper saves trees and energy.

questions.q: What should you do with old batteries?
options: Take them to a special drop-off, not the regular trash
Put them in the recycle bin with cans
questions.explain: Batteries contain harmful materials and need special handling.

questions.q: Why is clean water important for a whole town?
options: Dirty water is fine for drinking
People, farms, and animals all need clean water to live
questions.explain: Clean water is needed for drinking, farming, and wildlife.

questions.q: Which action helps keep a lake clean?
options: Washing cars so runoff flows into the lake
Keeping soap, oil, and trash out of the water
questions.explain: What goes down drains and onto ground can reach lakes, so keep pollutants out.

questions.q: Planting trees along a river helps because...
options: roots push soil into the water
roots hold the soil and shade keeps the water cool for fish
questions.explain: Tree roots prevent erosion and shade keeps river water cool and healthy.

Using hot water for every tiny load
questions.explain: Full loads use water and energy wisely instead of wasting both on tiny loads.

questions.q: Which sentence is TRUE?
options: One person's choices never matter at all
Kids can help the planet with everyday choices
questions.explain: Everyday choices by kids and adults add up to big help for the planet.

questions.q: What is the main idea of this whole unit?
options: People can care for Earth by reducing, reusing, recycling, and protecting nature
questions.explain: Caring for our planet means wasting less and protecting air, water, land, and wildlife.
